|Part of your Weavings of Existence have taken a nearly irreversible leap away from the Loose Cover of an Absolute Complex True Source.|
|Part of your Weavings of Existence are stepping into the Strict Cover of an Absolute Complex True Source.|
|The light of your True Source is capable of surviving the transfer into the area designated as the Infinite Ravines.|
The information flowed freely as Noah felt the subtle, infinite shifts.
He could feel the freedom within strictness, the strength hidden within fragility.
It was paradoxical...and yet, he was drawing closer.
Closer to the place where the weavings of the Great Beyonder awaited.
|The Weavings of your Existence are arriving at a region within the Infinite Ravines.|
|This region has been analyzed and distinguished as the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality. |
| Here, an unknown Wild True Source permeates the Hollow Cascade.
The Causality of Existence is reversed constantly. |
|Cause follows effect.
Enemies may bleed before they are struck.
Time flows backward.
Weavings unwind.|
|Your True Source must adapt, or your very existence will become unwound.|

chapters.title: Chapter 3650 Exodus! I
paragraphs: The Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality.
This was the domain where the Great Beyonder resided.

Noah's weavings of existence trembled as the True Source of the Singed wrapped tightly around him—protecting him from the ravages of Causality itself. Upon his arrival, he felt his True Source being converged upon and pulled into this place with terrifying force.
It was as if the Source was being displaced, forced to exert its power only within the Infinite Ravines, and nowhere else.
He could resist it.

He knew that with his True Source Atlas of Existence, and the True Source of Existence itself, he might actually withstand this undeniable force—not because it was opposing his Source, but because it ensured that 99.9% of it would remain anchored in the endlessly vast regions of the Ravines, where even the concept of distance was a paradox.
But for now, he allowed himself to flow with it.
Within moments, his weavings buzzed, and he fully crossed from The Weave into a new domain.
A domain that instantly caused his True Source to flare, white-gold flames of the Singed erupting protectively around him as the atmosphere trembled with existence-altering force.
"This..."
He heard his voice.
But he hadn't opened his mouth yet.
His lips parted only a breath later, and in that moment, he understood.
He had truly arrived in the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality.
The effect had occurred before the cause.
He heard himself before speaking.

And more than that—if his True Source hadn't instinctively enveloped him, his weavings of existence would already be destabilizing. Time flowed in every direction here. Without protection, the Wild True Source of this domain would begin to unravel a being, regressing them to the point they'd never even been born!
HUUM!
His surroundings buzzed with the weight of compressed paradox.
Then slowly...they came into focus.
Noah stood upon a field of stellar grains, silver-purple sands that shimmered like ground-down stars.
All around him...
Shattered Crystalline Megalos Seas floated in space. Rivers and waterfalls surged upward from them—flowing into the skies, crashing into floating landmasses and suspended lakes.
And the sky...
The Weaver of Existence buzzed loudly, displaying exactly what Noah was seeing.
[Skies of the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality. A dome of reflected true and false futures of causality. Some are real. Others are deceptive, born from the Wild True Source of Causality.]
Above, light-years away, layers of complex illusions pulsed constantly.
Some showed the lands breaking apart in one timeline. Others showed them untouched. And others still...showed himself.
Illusory figures of Noah appeared in the distant skies, flickering across divergent threads and possibilities.
One scene showed his golden flaming robes fluttering—then unraveling, along with his body.
Another showed him flying through the Cascade, only to be struck with the terrifying consequence of failure here.
Chrono-Fragmentation.
In that thread, his mind and existence were pulled into infinite possibility loops, spiraling endlessly into what-ifs until even his weavings began to collapse in on themselves.
Yet another illusory thread showed him standing still as a dark-haired woman materialized beside him, scoffing.
Her voice arrived before her figure.
And then...
He heard a voice that was oddly familiar.
"My dear Wild True Source of Causality... I thought we were getting along by now. I've grown immune to your complexity after all these years. Why try to unravel my weavings again?"

"Now you bring the causality of the one man I've been with after eons? To what, trigger an emotional fluctuation? You should know I'm not some weak woman. That man hasn't been critical to me for eons, and even if he knows some good tricks with Dual Cultivation, I'll be fine even if he was gone. You don't need to use his image to deceive me."
The voice of the Great Beyonder echoed into Noah's ears before she'd even arrived.
She was clearly being drawn in by the presence of a dazzling True Source that shouldn't be here.
And yet...she didn't believe it was him.
She believed it was just another trick of reversed causality—another illusion from the Hollow Cascade meant to manipulate her.
BZZT!
Just ahead of Noah, standing on the shimmering sands of stellar grains...
A gorgeous figure emerged, radiating terrifying waves of complexity.
Her complexity felt vastly greater than Noah's in this moment—both pure and intricately woven.
And it all converged into a single woman:
Dark hair. Equally dark eyes.
A vivacious form wrapped in a stellar obsidian robe that glowed with trillions of True Source runes.
Her face carried the timeless weight of ancient beauty and age. As she appeared, she crossed her arms, shaking her head.
Her lips began to move—but Noah had already heard the words. Seconds ago.
Thanks to the temporal disarray of this place.
Her body shimmered with waves of her True Source as she stepped forward—defying the flow of reversed causality.
Noah prepared to hear her again before she even spoke. He didn't like this disjointedness.

His True Source of the Singed pulsed violently as it began burning away the interference in nearby reality. It scorched through the local reversal of speech, syncing future audio to match the present moment.
Like editing a future echo to match current lips, the effect stabilized.
And her words finally flowed in sync with her voice.

"I have to give it to you, Causality," she said with a smile, "you captured everything about him very well. But your illusions only work when a trace will of mine isn't standing beside the subject inside the weavings of the Wheel itself."
She stepped closer.
Her complexity spilled out like dark crimson waves, formed from trillions of floating Runes—each capable of erasing what she still believed to be an illusion.
But Noah simply smiled.
He didn't respond.
Not here.
Not in this region of the Infinite Ravines.
Instead, he used his body within the Amarantos Dream, where her Trace Will existed—and asked her.
"What if I really am right there with you... in the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality?"

chapters.title: Chapter 3651 Exodus! II
paragraphs: What if he was there?
He hadn't even asked this with his body, the one that was actually inside the Infinite Ravines.
No.
He asked it with his weavings inside the Wheel of Existence, and the Great Beyonder could not call that false!
And the moment he did...
The fair face of the Great Beyonder here in the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality changed.
Shock.
Disbelief.
And then, rising anger!
The seas of complex authorities rising around her erupted in heavy waves as she roared.
"You...YOU! I told you—!"
Her voice cracked with emotion, her eyes burning with a mixture of fury and disbelief as if she couldn't fathom that he would actually come here!
After she'd explicitly told him not to.
His weavings could get locked down in this place.
His newly born True Source could be bound here.
And there was a rising enemy in the Wheel of Existence one only he could face.
He was their greatest hope.
But what had he done?
He had...
He had actually shown up.
Noah looked at the furious Great Beyonder—and as her full, unveiled complexity surged from her, he grew somber.
She was miles ahead of him it seemed. In raw complexity, in command of her True Source.
She could actually suppress the very structure of his True Source of the Singed if he didn't explain himself here.
So, he did with one sentence.
Enough to stop all doubt.
"I have two True Sources."
The billowing form of the raging Great Beyonder froze, millions of Runes flashing within her eyes as they sharpened and turned icy.
"...What?"
Noah simply repeated himself, as if it were the most natural thing in the world.
"I have two True Sources. One is here. One is already battling the Dead Thing inside the Wheel right now."
The dark sea of trillions of complex Runes around her stilled.
Her eyes churned with disbelief, suspicion, and confusion, but she didn't speak.
She had seen so much.
Over the years, she'd witnessed wonders. Faced impossibilities and walked through layers of existence most beings couldn't fathom.
She had ruled in the Megalos Beyond, dominated multiple Frequencies, and had an unfathomable Outerversal Lineage flowing through her blood.
She had seen countless complexities.
But this?
Two True Sources of Existence?
She didn't say anything at first.
Her mind was always open to possibilities...but this?
This was unthinkable.
Noah sighed.
He raised a hand.
His True Source of the Singed pulsed, burning away the reversed causality in their immediate space.
He summoned an illusory image, and there he was.
Fighting Bob.
His other self appeared as his form was wrapped in the stellar allure of a True Source of Existence, black halos spilling seas of reality into space.
Across from him, Bob—his body pulsing with Khaos was tearing existence apart!
With every blow exchanged, they shattered entire Frequencies, ripping across the Weave and only to reappear elsewhere right after.
And this whole time?
Bob had only been using Khaos.
The black and white Wheels behind him hadn't even been fully activated yet.
Noah was waiting and preparing for when they were utilized!
The Great Beyonder watched it all with pitch black eyes.
She shook her head, staring at him like he was an alien!
"Inconceivable...multiple True Sources? That's the very foundation and definition of a being. To have more than one, it should be unstable and impossible. How were you...?"
Her eyes narrowed sharply, glowing with dangerous curiosity.
She examined him, top to bottom.
Noah didn't answer her gaze.
Instead, he asked.
"Tell me about the Infinite Ravines and where we are right now. I'm curious about the Dead Things here."
He had tried spreading his weavings far—but the Wild True Source of Causality resisted.
Here, the farther you stretched, the more violent the pushback as there were limits.
But more than that, he was curious about the structure of the Ravines themselves.
Too vast for even the idea of distance!
The Great Beyonder watched him.
Still quiet.
Still processing.
Then finally...
"I don't understand you."
She said it quietly.
"I don't understand you, but if you say you have two True Sources...then you have two. I won't deny impossibilities as we are in desperate need of them."
WAA!
She raised her right hand, motioning to everything around them.
"I welcome you to the Gateway Domus of the Wheel of Existence, The Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality."
"Your weavings were unique enough to find this place without having to trace the flow of the Wheel."
Her tone shifted and became serious and grim.
"Places like this, Gateway Domus, they're unknown in number, but in the past few eons...many have been closed off and merged into others."
She continued.

"Think of the Gateway Domus as massive doors. If one of those doors is about to break, if it's about to be breached by a Dead Thing, the Wheel merges it with another because the Wheel can't just...close the door."
"The Infinite Ravines is made up of these Doors, and do you know why they're being merged?"
She asked the question.
Noah didn't hesitate as he sighed and nodded.
"Because the defenders of those Gateway Domus were either defeated or no longer there."
Defeated.
Or gone.
Legends- beings who had once achieved their True Source!
The Great Beyonder nodded slowly, closing her eyes.
"Yes. Half and half. Some fell, and some were worn down by time...or waves of Dead Things.

And others, they just left. An exodus of True Sources. They had defended for millions of years and faced endless assaults, and now, they grew tired and left. So now, Gateway Domus collapse and merge. Two Wild True Sources can be in one place. It becomes harder for Dead Things to breach, but also harder for any defender to maintain integrity."

"And the Wheel? It moves with logic and calculates what's necessary. If it sees a door is failing, it merges it based on who's inside. It measures complexity and sees if those within can handle the merge. If so, it proceeds as things are that dire."
She turned to him, voice sharp again.
"And now that you're here, the complexity of this Gateway Domus has changed. What the Wheel thought this door could handle has changed. I wouldn't be surprised if-...!
HUUUUM!
As if existence itself wanted to prove her right.
The Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality began to shake.

chapters.title: Chapter 3652 A Fortified Door! I
paragraphs: The Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality was shaking with interminable brilliance.
Noah's eyes were luminous as he scanned the surroundings, the words of the Great Beyonder echoing in his mind.
The Wheel of Existence could only be accessed through the Infinite Ravines, and the Ravines themselves were composed of countless doors known as Gateway Domus.

Depending on the intricacies of existence protecting a given Door, the Wheel could merge two Domus into one—for no reason other than one being on the verge of collapse, or the Defender of that Door no longer being able to hold the line.
His arrival at this particular Gateway Domus—the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality—had caused the Wheel to reevaluate its strength.
And now, it was likely that another Gateway Domus was being merged into it.
The Great Beyonder observed the shaking space and slowly shook her head, weariness and sorrow in her expression.

"The only reason the Wheel would act this aggressively, merging different doors, is if either the exodus of the long-standing Defenders has increased, or the Dead Things hammering at those Doors are growing stronger."

"I've remained in these Cascades of Reversed Causality for eons without change. So I suppose I should thank you—for being the catalyst of all this right now. I only hope we survive it. Until now, I've been defending against a few Dead Things, attacking in sequence. But they've sensed the shift after all of this. They will come in full force now. And with another Gateway Domus merging here, we'll also face an unknown number of Dead Things from that doorway. I just hope it's one that had a protector—someone simply deemed not strong enough—rather than an empty Gateway Domus. Because if it's empty...their burden falls entirely on us."
Two scenarios.
It wasn't clear which would become their reality. But as the trembling of the Hollow Cascade reached its peak, a sharp crack echoed through the void—existence itself splintering to their right.

Light-years away, it looked as though reality was folding in on itself. The silver-purple stellar weavings that defined this space of reversed causality began to darken—interwoven with dim black seas.
Seas filled with obsidian vines, writhing outward and snaring everything in their reach.
Two Gateway Domus were merging, with the new one burning with tenebrous radiance as its vines looked vile and filled with horror.
|The Gateway Domus blooming ahead has been deemed the Absolute Fear of Existence...|

His weavings spun rapidly, decoding its nature as he spoke to the Great Beyonder—who now stood rigid while trillions of Runes were spiraling from her being to verify the aura of the new Domus being integrated.
Noah's role as the Weaver of Existence surged to life, sensing the identity of the new doorway forming.
|The Gateway Domus blooming ahead has been deemed the Absolute Fear of Existence...|

His weavings spun rapidly, decoding its nature as he spoke to the Great Beyonder—who now stood rigid while trillions of Runes were spiraling from her being to verify the aura of the new Domus being integrated.

"The merging Gateway Domus is the Absolute Fear of Existence. It carries the Wild True Source of Fear. Within its scope, every True Source will bear fruit to the user's deepest existential fear—and manifest it. Anyone inside will face their own worst nightmare...endlessly amplified by the Source."
A dreadful Domus.
The manifestation of the worst fear of True Source Entities!
Just what fear could a being like the True Beyonder have, and what manifestation of fear would be expressed for Noah?

The Great Beyonder, analyzing it with her entire being, turned toward Noah in stunned silence. She had only just identified the Domus, and not even begun to understand its inner workings—yet Noah had already discerned the Wild True Source it housed.
Her Complexity was far greater than his—yet he saw it first.
Her gaze narrowed sharply.
"Yes, and—...!"
But her words faltered.
Because the shaking intensified, growing more violent. Both Noah and the Great Beyonder turned their heads—not to the right, where the Fear Domus merged—but to the left.
Another weaving of existence was descending.
Another Gateway Domus was being merged.
The Great Beyonder went pale.
Noah's eyes hardened.

"This... this shouldn't be happening. My Complexity is far higher than yours. Why the fuck would the Wheel merge not one but two additional Gateway Domus just because you stepped in?! What the fuck?!"
The Great Beyonder's fury rose as realization dawned—three Gateway Domus were converging into one.

To their left, pure white bled into everything. Endless white corridors emerged, hallways blooming outward into a maze-like structure as Noah observed it with grave intensity, his distinction as the Weaver of Existence going to work once more!

"This is the Pale Verbum Labyrinth. It's suffused with the Wild True Source of Verbum. Within its walls, no one can unleash their True Source through traditional means—only through their words. Every word must carry intent. Every sentence must be structured. Speak recklessly, and your power withers. Speak with precision, and you may command a thousand times the strength of your True Source. In that Domus... silence means annihilation."
Even Noah's eyes pulsed at the thought. The Great Beyonder's full attention swung to him now, unreadable emotion behind her tired gaze.

"I've been here for millions of years," she whispered. "And nothing changed. Then you step in, and within minutes, the Wheel decides to merge two more Domus into this one? Every Domus is a path. That means we're about to face an influx of Dead Things from three different fronts! And we haven't even seen another Defender yet—!"
Her voice cut off once more.
Both she and Noah turned—gazes locking onto the twisting white corridors still forming.
From one of them, a vibrant True Source bloomed. Not wild. Controlled. Ancient.

Footsteps echoed. A figure in white robes emerged, his eyes shimmering with the brilliance of endless stars. And as the Great Beyonder saw him, she trembled—her voice cracking with recognition and slight easing as if she felt their weight lessen somewhat.
"Veyl'Aethra!"
A name.
A legend.
She spoke it like a memory.
He looked nothing like a warrior—just an old man with kind eyes and a smile, protected by a unique True Source that wrapped him like a cloak of existence.
And he came to stand, calmly, at the junction between the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality and the Pale Verbum Labyrinth.
A legend Noah had never even heard of—yet one who now stood as the second Defender of the Infinite Ravines that he had met here!

sentences.text: The Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality was shaking with interminable brilliance.
Noah's eyes were luminous as he scanned the surroundings, the words of the Great Beyonder echoing in his mind.
The Wheel of Existence could only be accessed through the Infinite Ravines, and the Ravines themselves were composed of countless doors known as Gateway Domus.

Depending on the intricacies of existence protecting a given Door, the Wheel could merge two Domus into one—for no reason other than one being on the verge of collapse, or the Defender of that Door no longer being able to hold the line.
His arrival at this particular Gateway Domus—the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality—had caused the Wheel to reevaluate its strength.
And now, it was likely that another Gateway Domus was being merged into it.
The Great Beyonder observed the shaking space and slowly shook her head, weariness and sorrow in her expression.

"The only reason the Wheel would act this aggressively, merging different doors, is if either the exodus of the long-standing Defenders has increased, or the Dead Things hammering at those Doors are growing stronger."
"I've remained in these Cascades of Reversed Causality for eons without change.
So I suppose I should thank you—for being the catalyst of all this right now.
I only hope we survive it.
Until now, I've been defending against a few Dead Things, attacking in sequence.
But they've sensed the shift after all of this.
They will come in full force now.
And with another Gateway Domus merging here, we'll also face an unknown number of Dead Things from that doorway.
I just hope it's one that had a protector—someone simply deemed not strong enough—rather than an empty Gateway Domus.
Because if it's empty...their burden falls entirely on us."
Two scenarios.
It wasn't clear which would become their reality.
But as the trembling of the Hollow Cascade reached its peak, a sharp crack echoed through the void—existence itself splintering to their right.
Light-years away, it looked as though reality was folding in on itself.
The silver-purple stellar weavings that defined this space of reversed causality began to darken—interwoven with dim black seas.
Seas filled with obsidian vines, writhing outward and snaring everything in their reach.
Two Gateway Domus were merging, with the new one burning with tenebrous radiance as its vines looked vile and filled with horror.
|The Gateway Domus blooming ahead has been deemed the Absolute Fear of Existence...|

His weavings spun rapidly, decoding its nature as he spoke to the Great Beyonder—who now stood rigid while trillions of Runes were spiraling from her being to verify the aura of the new Domus being integrated.
Noah's role as the Weaver of Existence surged to life, sensing the identity of the new doorway forming.
|The Gateway Domus blooming ahead has been deemed the Absolute Fear of Existence...|

His weavings spun rapidly, decoding its nature as he spoke to the Great Beyonder—who now stood rigid while trillions of Runes were spiraling from her being to verify the aura of the new Domus being integrated.
"The merging Gateway Domus is the Absolute Fear of Existence.
It carries the Wild True Source of Fear.
Within its scope, every True Source will bear fruit to the user's deepest existential fear—and manifest it.
Anyone inside will face their own worst nightmare...endlessly amplified by the Source."
A dreadful Domus.
The manifestation of the worst fear of True Source Entities!
Just what fear could a being like the True Beyonder have, and what manifestation of fear would be expressed for Noah?
The Great Beyonder, analyzing it with her entire being, turned toward Noah in stunned silence.
She had only just identified the Domus, and not even begun to understand its inner workings—yet Noah had already discerned the Wild True Source it housed.
Her Complexity was far greater than his—yet he saw it first.
Her gaze narrowed sharply.
"Yes, and—...!"
But her words faltered.
Because the shaking intensified, growing more violent.
Both Noah and the Great Beyonder turned their heads—not to the right, where the Fear Domus merged—but to the left.
Another weaving of existence was descending.
Another Gateway Domus was being merged.
The Great Beyonder went pale.
Noah's eyes hardened.
"This... this shouldn't be happening.
My Complexity is far higher than yours.
Why the fuck would the Wheel merge not one but two additional Gateway Domus just because you stepped in?!
What the fuck?!"
The Great Beyonder's fury rose as realization dawned—three Gateway Domus were converging into one.
To their left, pure white bled into everything.
Endless white corridors emerged, hallways blooming outward into a maze-like structure as Noah observed it with grave intensity, his distinction as the Weaver of Existence going to work once more!
"This is the Pale Verbum Labyrinth.
It's suffused with the Wild True Source of Verbum.
Within its walls, no one can unleash their True Source through traditional means—only through their words.
Every word must carry intent.
Every sentence must be structured.
Speak recklessly, and your power withers.
Speak with precision, and you may command a thousand times the strength of your True Source.
In that Domus... silence means annihilation."
Even Noah's eyes pulsed at the thought.
The Great Beyonder's full attention swung to him now, unreadable emotion behind her tired gaze.
"I've been here for millions of years," she whispered.
"And nothing changed.
Then you step in, and within minutes, the Wheel decides to merge two more Domus into this one?
Every Domus is a path.
That means we're about to face an influx of Dead Things from three different fronts!
And we haven't even seen another Defender yet—!"
Her voice cut off once more.
Both she and Noah turned—gazes locking onto the twisting white corridors still forming.
From one of them, a vibrant True Source bloomed.
Not wild.
Controlled.
Ancient.
Footsteps echoed.
A figure in white robes emerged, his eyes shimmering with the brilliance of endless stars.
And as the Great Beyonder saw him, she trembled—her voice cracking with recognition and slight easing as if she felt their weight lessen somewhat.
"Veyl'Aethra!"
A name.
A legend.
She spoke it like a memory.
He looked nothing like a warrior—just an old man with kind eyes and a smile, protected by a unique True Source that wrapped him like a cloak of existence.
And he came to stand, calmly, at the junction between the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality and the Pale Verbum Labyrinth.
A legend Noah had never even heard of—yet one who now stood as the second Defender of the Infinite Ravines that he had met here!

chapters.title: Chapter 3653 A Fortified Door! II
paragraphs: Legends.
There were an unknown number of them. The ones Noah knew were simply those who shone the brightest in this most recent era.

But across Frequencies, there existed others—ancient legends who lived eons upon eons ago. They had long since attained their True Sources. Like many before and after them, they had once sensed the pull of the Infinite Ravines—a place that could amplify their Complexity...but also trap them here for eons to come.
The one who arrived at this moment was someone Noah had never seen before.
But the Great Beyonder knew him very well.
She leaned close and whispered only for him to hear, filling him in.

"Veyl'Aethra, the Oracle of Collapse. His True Source is Chronotropy—he specializes in unraveling time and existence itself. He can age Sources and concepts, erode causality, even collapse the entire sensation of time for others—locking them into existential stasis for eons. Many of us believed he was dead. He was generations behind me, the Stellar Weaver, or that wanker, the Omnifather."
She spoke plainly, though her words ended on a name laced with derision—and even a flicker of anger.
The Omnifather.
Noah glanced at her and asked, still studying the distant legend with sharp intent—intent on seeing if he could study the True Source and integrate it into his own.
"Why does the Omnifather earn the title of wanker?"
His question drew a sharp huff from the Great Beyonder as she shot forward toward the Pale Verbum Labyrinth, her voice echoing behind her.

"Who do you think tried to break back into the Wheel of Existence and accidentally brought a Dead Thing with him? Even after sacrificing a large part of his True Source to hunt it down, the damage was done. His actions caused the chaos inside the Wheel."
The Omnifather.
He was responsible for the discovery—and eventual extinction—of the Megalonians.
And now, his recklessness had affected the Wheel of Existence itself.
Noah's eyes brightened as he recalled the Remnant Weavings of the Omnifather—the one he'd spoken to before extracting the Source of Versality.
Even then, he seemed aware of Faceless Lifeforms and what they represented.
He was the one who had inadvertently allowed Bob into the Wheel of Existence!
This guy...had a tendency to cause problems.
He was responsible for the discovery—and eventual extinction—of the Megalonians.
And now, his recklessness had affected the Wheel of Existence itself.
Noah shook his head as he arrived beside the Great Beyonder, facing Veyl'Aethra and his ever-dramatic name that was far too much of a mouthful. The Great Beyonder spoke out.
"Sir, it's an honor to fight beside you. Are you alone? How many Dead Things usually assault this place?"
Her voice was direct—seeking critical answers without delay.

The old man in white robes smiled wearily, stepping out of the Pale Verbum Labyrinth, where words bore terrifying power. When he spoke, his voice was deep and majestic. From his very presence—and the silent pulse of his Source—Noah felt a profound purity and complexity that surpassed even the Great Beyonder.

"Five little fiends have tried to break me over the eons. Their Dead True Sources are nearing collapse, growing more desperate. It seems the Wheel believes I can no longer endure what's to come. So now, I join you—one I've heard about from the whispers of talkative others—and this...new one, it seems?"
His gaze settled on Noah as the Great Beyonder's expression grew more somber. She nodded slowly.
Five Dead Things.
She herself faced three that routinely clawed their way through the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality. The number had nearly doubled.
Worse, her eyes drifted toward the distant edge of the Domus of Absolute Fear of Existence as her voice dropped low.
"Five from you, three from me...and an unknown number from the Gateway Domus of Absolute Fear of Existence. And it seems—no Defender is coming out of that one."
One of the worst-case scenarios.
A Domus merged into theirs—and already without a Defender.
Either its guardian had left or had been killed.
The air turned unbearably heavy. Then—
HUUM!
The junction between the Domus of Absolute Fear of Existence, the Pale Verbum Labyrinth, and the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality collapsed into convergence.
And all weavings of existence among the three Domus fully melded, fusing into a single space.
Three Wild True Sources ignited and clashed—Causality, Fear, and Verbum—their effects compounding in real-time, covering entire light-years in chaos and raw, unpredictable power of Existence.
Noah stood at the center of it all, his weavings absorbing every detail, his focus razor-sharp as he analyzed both threats and opportunities.
Then—
AWUU!
A howl erupted from the Pale Verbum Labyrinth.
A scream layered with death and destruction. It came from weavings saturated in ancient hatred—weavings tired of everything, desiring only endings.
Veyl'Aethra shook his head grimly as he spoke.

"The Dead Thing Yrrmoth, the Maw of the Unwritten, is the first to sense the convergence and arrive. Last time I saw it, I fought it alongside another Dead Thing. But as it sensed its death approaching, it turned on its ally—devoured it. It must have finished assimilating what it gained. And now... its complexity has likely surpassed what I can withstand. That's why the Wheel decided I could no longer defend the Pale Verbum Labyrinth alone."
The Oracle of Collapse's expression darkened.
And Noah's eyes flared as the monstrous entity approached—light-years away—shattering the stretching white corridors as it advanced.
It looked like a skeletal serpent, its body inscribed with glyphs that pulsed with malevolence.
Veyl'Aethra continued, speaking for the benefit of the two beside him.

"Yrrmoth, the Maw of the Unwritten, holds the Dead True Source of Obliviscript. It devours stories, existence, even opposing True Sources. If your Source is not properly shielded, it will consume the lore and meaning of your being. Protect your record. Protect your story. And be careful with your words. In overlapping regions, you may still express your Source freely, but in others—those governed by the Pale Verbum Labyrinth—you will need words to channel power. Stand tall, O Defenders of the Wheel. For this... is only the beginning. Surviving this and what comes next will reveal exactly why the Wheel has done what it has."
Words wrapped in shimmering weavings of existence fell from Veyl'Aethra's lips as Noah prepared to face yet another Dead Thing since Bob!

chapters.title: Chapter 3654 Adaptation! I
paragraphs: Yrrmoth, the Maw of the Unwritten.

A dead thing wielding the forsaken True Source of Obliviscript—a Source capable of consuming lore itself, erasing the very meaning of one's existence. Against such a force, even a bearer of a True Source could find their essence fading, their reality unthreaded if they lacked the power to resist Obliviscript.

A monstrous entity, skeletal and serpentine, covered in glyphs etched into bone, tore through the pale white halls and corridors of the Pale Verbum Labyrinth. Nearby, Noah, the Great Beyonder, and Veyl'Aethra, the Oracle of Collapse who wielded the True Source of Chronotropy, prepared for what approached.
Amidst that preparation, the dark hair of the Great Beyonder shimmered as she turned to Noah and spoke.

"Before that Dead Thing gets here, I want to get a better grasp of your power—and your complexity. I need to understand why the Wheel would do something so drastic, and why now. Tell me, what do you know about the levels of power and complexity among those of us who've obtained a True Source?"
Even as a dead thing barreled toward them, they conversed—because beings of their caliber could hold entire conversations in the space of a single moment, stretching seconds into what felt like days.
Communication flowed like lightning as in mere instants, they could exchange volumes.
The Great Beyonder was doing exactly that, ensuring she understood the power of the being who had entered this domain—one who claimed to possess two True Sources.
Noah gave her a slight nod before replying with ease.
"Why don't you enlighten me?"
The complexity of those who had attained a True Source.
The Weaver of Existence was already quantifying such metrics under Noah's terms—but there was no harm in incorporating what the current Weavings of Existence defined as complexity.
The Great Beyonder's eyes glinted as she looked toward the distant Yrrmoth, who now broke apart the Wild True Source of Verbum while surging toward them like a hurricane of decay.

"When one obtains a True Source, they're considered to have reached a benchmark that few beings among the countless under the Wheels of Existence ever attain. It's a pinnacle of power. It means that someone, within their lifetime, achieved something monumental. And yet, in terms of complexity, someone who's just awakened their Source is known as a Nascent Source-Bearer."
Nascent Source-Bearer.
The Great Beyonder uttered the term with clarity, gesturing toward Noah as if to confirm that was what he currently was.
Veyl'Aethra watched their exchange with a silent smile.
The Great Beyonder continued.

"A Nascent Source-Bearer earns that title based on their Complexity and Purity. These two traits—Complexity and Purity—are fundamental. It doesn't matter how powerful someone appears; if they lack in either, they'll never truly ascend. If one has great Complexity but low Purity, their power stagnates. At the Nascent Source-Bearer level, you can command your Source to pass through the Infinite Ravines, even survive without the shelter of a Wheel. You can challenge Wild True Sources and clash with other True Source entities of similar standing."

"To overcome another Nascent Source-Bearer, your own Source must either be of an extraordinarily high tier, possessing elevated Purity and Complexity, or be uniquely compatible. Most Nascent Bearers have average levels in both. So then—how does one grow stronger? How do you refine your Purity and Complexity?"
She asked, her voice threaded with challenge.
Noah remained calm, pointing toward the chaotic Wild True Sources whirling around them.
"A place like the Infinite Ravines helps."
Yes.
A place like the Infinite Ravines.
The Great Beyonder nodded in agreement.
"Yes. One of the methods for increasing one's Complexity and Purity is something we call... Existential Source Trials."
A methodology for enhancing one's True Source—Existential Source Trials.

"When your Source is exposed to and withstands other Sources—especially Wild True Sources—over time, it adapts. It's like being struck by hammers of raw existence, over and over again. Each blow tries to break you. Every time you survive, you come out stronger. That's what an Existential Source Trial is—a relentless battering of your essence until it evolves enough to challenge many others."

"This is the path most of us walk in the Infinite Ravines. Even I have reforged my Source through it. After fighting Dead Things over and over again, enduring the Wild True Source of Causality across countless millennia... I escaped the bounds of a Nascent Source-Bearer and became...a Harmonized Sourcebound Icon."
WAA!
The first two stages of True Source Entities were revealed.
Nascent Source-Bearer, and then Harmonized Sourcebound Icon!
Trillions of runes circled the Great Beyonder as she raised her hands, revealing a fraction of the power she'd cultivated through the harsh discipline of Purity and Complexity refinement.

"At this stage, one's True Source has matured to the point where it is recognized as having Moderate Purity and Moderate Complexity. We can easily surpass newly awakened Sources with lesser development. A hallmark of a Harmonized Sourcebound Icon is the ability to lay down a Pillar of Concordance—an imprint of one's Source that spreads through external existence. A projection of power, purified and harmonized, that can convert a region across light-years to reflect the law of your own Source."

"It's as if you've built your own Domus—a stable realm, no longer ruled by Wild True Sources, but governed by your own. And when a Dead Thing arrives? It must fight you on your terms. It must contend with your Source. That is how I've survived these countless years inside the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality."
The Great Beyonder had survived for millions of years because she had attained the second distinction among those who obtained their True Source.

She had become a Harmonized Sourcebound Icon, capable of laying down a Pillar of Concordance—a manifestation of the philosophy and purpose behind her True Source—unleashing its Purity and Complexity to turn an entire region into her own Domus- her own source with its unique impositions of existence!
Where every being who dared to breach it had to withstand the very essence her True Source represented.

chapters.title: Chapter 3655 Adaptation! II
paragraphs: "It takes very little authority from our True Source to enact the Pillar of Concordance, but it's one of the supreme weapons available to entities at our level. Any being seeking to survive within a Gateway Domus of the Wheel and defend it must obtain this level of power. Some of us are fortunate enough to grow into it without being ground down to nothingness, while others... they don't have the time. And so, they seek other paths to acquire such power. That brings us to the second methodology for obtaining a higher level of Complexity."
The Great Beyonder chose her words carefully. Noah raised an eyebrow, catching something unspoken in her tone, and asked lightly.
"Only Complexity? This other method... it doesn't raise Purity?"
She hadn't mentioned Purity.
Only Complexity.
And now, she nodded slowly, the weight of the truth settling in her eyes.

"Yes. The first Mechanic of Ascension to elevate a True Source is the Existential Source Trials. The second... is Source Devouring Evolution. It has two components, but only one of them truly works—and that's Complexity Devouring. It focuses solely on Complexity. Through this method, one can devour the Weavings of Wild True Sources, Living True Sources, or even Dead True Sources to rapidly increase Complexity. The fastest method is devouring Living True Sources, followed by Dead True Sources, and then Wild True Sources. But this method comes with a terrible cost—your Purity becomes corrupted. Tainted to an unimaginable degree. Your Source is stained by what you consume."
Her expression turned solemn, and a shadow flickered in her eyes—something heavy, burdened by history and sorrow.

"That is why they are drawn to the Infinite Ravines—any Absolute Complex True Source of Existence can nourish them. Even the Wild True Sources that dwell within can sustain them. But there's a terrifying drawback to devouring any Source indiscriminately and weaving it into your own. True Sources are too powerful. You risk corruption, existential collapse... even the complete loss of identity. When it gets truly bad—when your Source becomes a tangled mess of incompatible weavings—you face something called... Fractal Collapse."

"Some of our own people have taken this path, sacrificing the Purity of their True Source to gain more Complexity. If they raised their Complexity high enough, some were able to ascend into Harmonized Sourcebound Icons with a high level of Moderate Complexity...but with Below Average Purity, or even worse—Tainted Purity. This path is very, very dangerous. It's the one Dead Things follow most often. They will devour any trace of a True Source they can, because they have already accepted a predetermined death. And they will do anything to postpone it."

"That is why they are drawn to the Infinite Ravines—any Absolute Complex True Source of Existence can nourish them. Even the Wild True Sources that dwell within can sustain them. But there's a terrifying drawback to devouring any Source indiscriminately and weaving it into your own. True Sources are too powerful. You risk corruption, existential collapse... even the complete loss of identity. When it gets truly bad—when your Source becomes a tangled mess of incompatible weavings—you face something called... Fractal Collapse."
WAA!
Her voice trembled with memory, as if she were reliving something vile from a past too ancient to name.
Fractal Collapse.
Even Veyl'Aethra's face darkened at the mention of it.
The Great Beyonder continued.

"Fractal Collapse happens when a Source becomes increasingly complex but is paired with dangerously corrupted Purity. It leads to the formation of... Fractal True Sources of Existence. Fractal Beings. Most Dead Things you'll encounter are either on the brink of becoming one—or already are."
Her voice was somber.
She had just spoken in detail about one component of Source Devouring Evolution-Complexity Devouring.
Noah's Weavings buzzed with endless possibility. He couldn't help but ask.
"What's the second component of Source Devouring Evolution?"
The other mechanic.

The Great Beyonder shook her head, as if it were something not even worth mentioning. Still, she answered. Even as they spoke within the span of an instant, Yrrmoth—the Maw of the Unwritten—was still inching closer within that very same breath of time.

"The second component... is Purity Devouring. It involves finding a complementary and similar True Source of Existence, then devouring its likeness—its resonance—to your own. But this is nearly impossible. Every True Source is unique. To find one that matches yours exactly... it almost never happens. But if someone is lucky enough to encounter a True Source similar to theirs, they can siphon its Purity and rapidly increase their own, gaining a slight boost in Complexity as well. Still... it's so rare."
Too rare.

There has only ever been a single case—a True Source Entity who arrived in the Infinite Ravines and, by unimaginable chance, encountered a Wild True Source in a Gateway Domus that matched their own forged Source. They were able to siphon its Purity and Complexity, rising to a level of power beyond even the Harmonized Sourcebound Icon.
But that was just one...
One being.
One moment of absurd luck.
As Noah listened, he glanced toward the wild resources around this Domus, thoughts spinning.

He wanted to voice something—to ask the Great Beyonder that what if someone could forge a second True Source to match the Wild True Source around them? Wouldn't they then be able to siphon off its Purity freely?
But even if he asked... he knew the answer. He'd be met with skepticism. Others held only one True Source.

Unless they shattered their current Source and began anew—rebuilding from nothing, carefully matching the Wild True Source in their environment—they wouldn't be able to. And even then, they would never survive the ravaging process long enough to see it through.
But he could.
HUUM!
His mind hummed with Tyranny.
His Weavings sparked with infinite potential.
He already carried the Weavings of Causality—it was a Pathway now.
Could he not continue?
Could he not forge multiple, compatible True Sources—each harmonized with Wild True Sources and even the Sources of others—so that he could seamlessly ascend in both Complexity and Purity?
The ideas buzzing in his mind made the Weavings of his existence leap with anticipation, vibrating as if they were already grasping the future.
Nascent Source-Bearer Complexity. Harmonized Sourcebound Icon Complexity.
The Mechanic of Ascension, Existential Source Trials.
The Mechanic of Ascension, Source Devouring Evolution with its twin paths—Complexity Devouring and Purity Devouring.
All of it danced through his thoughts. Plans and possibilities began to take shape—visions even the Great Beyonder hadn't imagined.

chapters.title: Chapter 3656 Adaptation! III
paragraphs: As The Great Beyonder finished explaining the mechanics for elevating the Complexity and Purity of a True Source—and the kinds of power one could wield at each level—she turned toward him, her voice quiet, intent.

"So, knowing all of this, you should at least not be caught off guard when you meet Dead Things. And it begs the question—why your entrance here led to all of this. I could feel your Complexity clearly... but Purity? That's different. One's Purity is always hidden, no matter their level of power. That's the only explanation circling in my mind for why the Wheel of Existence would do what it just did. You must have a secret. Maybe... a level of Purity I can't comprehend. I don't know your limits. So, the only thing I can propose is this—test them."
A test of his limits.
A test of his Purity.
He already knew—his Purity was incomparable. Because he had done something none of them ever had.
He had severed every single concept he had taken as a Pathway—eighty-one times—before forging it into a Source.
Eighty-one severings for every single Pathway. With the level of Purity he had achieved, there shouldn't be another being in existence who could match him at the same level.
Was that what the Wheel of Existence had considered when it chose to merge two Gateway Domus into the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality?
"My friends," Veyl'Aethra's calm voice rang out. "I believe our time is up."

In the midst of their conversation, Veyl'Aethra turned toward the distance—toward the serpentine skeletal form of Yrrmoth diving through the Wild True Source of Verbum, its body now weaving itself into the Wild True Source of Causality.
The white robes of the old man shifted as he sensed Yrrmoth's elevation in power, his voice soft and haunting—like a lullaby.

"Yrrmoth, the Maw of the Unwritten... it seems to have devoured the other Source that had been assaulting me. And now... its Purity is so corrupted, it's displaying the first sign of a Fractal Collapse of Existence—Echo Distortion."
A sign of an approaching Fractal Being.
Noah narrowed his eyes at the oncoming Yrrmoth. The massive, skeletal serpent rippled strangely, its form fizzling at the edges—as if its existence lagged in real time.
One moment, it was a pristine white skeleton and the next, its body spasmed, covered in fur and then scales—never settling down to one single thing.
It couldn't hold its form!

Echo Distortion. The Purity of the devoured Source was now clashing against its own, threatening to dismantle the very identity of the being it once was as its Dead True Source was put under scrutiny.
And this...was just one Dead Thing.
Veyl'Aethra exhaled a heavy breath, stepping forward until he stood between Noah and the Great Beyonder. With a graceful wave of his hand, something glorious appeared.
Between them and Yrrmoth...
A bloom of terrifyingly complex energy surged as Noah witnessed the rise of a massive, incandescent pillar of radiant purple light.
A Pillar of Concordance.

That one gesture confirmed what he already suspected- Veyl'Aethra was a Harmonized Sourcebound Icon. From the place where he stood, the pillar stretched outward, consuming regions heavy with the Wild True Sources of Causality and Verbum.
The brilliance bloomed like violet purple petals—petals that bore the hands of time, shattered clock faces, and spinning wheels etched with the runes of Chronotropy.
It was breathtaking.
This was the Pillar of Concordance of Chronotropy—and its very identity was rewriting the rules of reality in front of them.
But Veyl'Aethra had only cast it forward. He kept it from touching the Weavings of Noah and the Great Beyonder.
Still, the display was extraordinary.
As Yrrmoth entered the field of violet light, its skeletal form roared in anguish, pulsing with white flame.
White and violet collided.
The skeletal serpent surged forward through unraveling time and space, pressing toward the towering pillar—over light-years tall—stretching into wonder above and below.
And yet...
Despite swimming endlessly through this purple sea of shattered clocks and flickering timelines—it wasn't advancing.
It wasn't moving at all.
No matter how hard it surged, it remained in place.
A terrifying distortion of existence.
Noah turned sharply toward Veyl'Aethra, whose expression had gone ice cold.
"It will keep coming," he said flatly, "but it will never arrive."
HUUM!
Coming—but never arriving.
Yrrmoth thrashed, endlessly reaching for a destination he could see... but could never reach.
It howled, fury and desperation converging, as a Pillar began to rise from its own corrupted Source.
A budding Pillar of Concordance!
The Great Beyonder's gaze sharpened, her expression darkening. She floated forward, trillions of runes gathering around her.
With quiet power, she spoke.
"Pillar of Concordance."
A black pillar unfurled from her body, made of swirling runes and rippling existence.
And yet...it didn't overlap with the Pillar of Chronotropy.
It did not move to reinforce the Oracle of Collapse!
Instead, it reached toward the opposite end—where the Wild True Sources of Causality and Fear flowed freely.
Because from that direction... she sensed something new.
Two more unique signatures.
Two more Dead Things.
They had sensed Yrrmoth—something with a resonance like theirs—and had responded.
Two more entities emerged from the direction of the Wild True Source of Fear.
These weren't known. No defenders from their origin Domus had ever reached this side.
Even the Great Beyonder didn't recognize them.
Her expression twisted with somberness as her obsidian pillar surged, casting her influence across light-years of existence.
And then—another tremor.
Her eyes snapped toward another direction.
Two more Dead Things.
These, she knew. They were among the trio that frequently assaulted the Gateway Domus of Causality.
One became five.
The eyes of the Great Beyonder flickered with doubt—and resolve. She turned toward Noah, her voice deadly serious.
"If ever there was a time to reveal something—some unique secret, some hidden power—it is now. Before our very Sources are threatened. Before we stand at the edge of collapse."
"Because these five Dead Things?"
"They might just be the first volley."

chapters.title: Chapter 3657 Adaptation! IV
paragraphs: Now was the time for him to reveal anything he had been hiding!
And perhaps reveal whatever it was that had caused the Wheel of Existence to merge multiple Gateway Domus together.
The Great Beyonder uttered those words softly, as Noah's weavings pulsed in quiet resonance.
Compared to others...what made him unique?
The answer rested entirely in his Purity.
One of his bodies, currently stationed in the True Frequency of the Singed, could feel the gaze of the Origin Singed. And from that being's eyes, he felt something rare.
Caution.
Not hostility—but caution. As if the Origin Singed could not fathom the level of Purity emanating from the True Source Noah had just obtained.
Of course, he held the True Source Atlas of Existence, among other things—but here, the Singed remained singular in its judgment.

Noah's path diverged from all others. While they ascended through Lesser Sources, Greater Sources, Prime Sources, and eventually the revered Undeniable Telos Prime Sources, before evolving into True Source Complexity Entities—
He had walked a different road.
He didn't climb through Amalgamation. He never cobbled together fragments.
He severed his Ordinances eighty-one times until they became Pathways.
And when he finally obtained a Source from the Pathway—it was already a True Source.
Noah's ascent was different. Profoundly so!
Naturally, his Purity didn't match the conventional metrics explained by the Great Beyonder.
Nascent Source-Bearer Complexity Entities were known to have Average Purity, but he could feel it- his Purity far exceeded those bounds.
It felt as though his Purity belonged among Harmonized Sourcebound Icon Complexities.
So.
He decided to test it.

His Weaver of Existence Distinction analyzed the Pillars of Concordance cast by both the Great Beyonder and Veyl'Aethra—pillars that had turned their surrounding regions into extensions of their True Source.
His gaze then turned to the distant silver seas and rising waterfalls of Causality, where two Dead Things now approached.
And he spoke, softly.
"Pillar."
HUUM!
The Great Beyonder's eyes flew open, astonished as she heard the first word. He didn't hesitate as he completed it.
"Of Concordance."
Three simple words.
But in the next breath—toward the direction from which the two Dead Things advanced...
A dazzling pillar of white-gold brilliance erupted.
It wasn't just flames.
This was a pillar of judgment.

A white-gold flaming monument that rippled across many light-years, rising and descending with seeming infinitude. It spread the weavings of its True Source across the domain of Causality—and just in time.
The two Dead Things were approaching.
The Great Beyonder turned toward Noah, her gaze unreadable.
He didn't even need to look back before he spoke.

"The Purity of my True Source may have just surpassed the distinction between Nascent Source-Bearer and Harmonized Sourcebound Icon. It seems... if Purity is high enough, even Average or Low Complexity can be overridden to exhibit power on par with higher-tiered beings."
He said it so casually.
The Great Beyonder and Veyl'Aethra exchanged glances.
The old man offered Noah a smile.
"It's always good to see the young ones outpacing us. But let's not celebrate yet—this is only a portion of the Dead Things making their way here. I still don't see how we'll survive the rest."
Yes.
Things were only beginning.
The Great Beyonder kept her sharp gaze fixed on Noah, speaking as she observed the two Dead Things surging toward the white-gold flaming domain where his Pillar of Concordance had been enacted.

"The ones approaching your True Source... I know them well. Nyxal, the Dreamer Beneath Withering Stars, bearer of the Dead True Source of Somnial Nihilum—a collapsed Source of dreams and imagination. And Grys, the Archivist of Hollow Truths, with the Dead True Source of Veritas Moribundum—a fossilized Source of Truth that corrupts certainty itself.
Both are tricky little fuckers. Will the Purity of your Source be enough against them?"
She asked a critical question, just as Nyxal and Grys entered Noah's expanded Pillar of Concordance of the Singed.
Nyxal's form was a titanic humanoid of ashen-gray flesh with five glowing eyes across his face.
Grys was a woman with an obsidian trident, her lower half a mass of writhing octopus-like tentacles.
The moment they breached Noah's domain, the white-gold flames surged wildly.
The flames latched onto the weavings of existence surrounding the two Dead Things—burning not with heat, but with the purity of eonic embers that could never be extinguished.
OOOH!
Roars of fury erupted from both beings.
Grys' corrupted Source shattered certainty in her surroundings, causing the white-gold flames to flicker in and out of reality.
Nyxal unleashed a source of endless, recursive dreams—powerful enough to trap even True Sources in endless loops, further disrupting the flames.
And yet...
They burned on.
Flickering, warping, but never fading.
They returned.
These were no ordinary flames.
They were the True Flames of the Singed, fueled by such terrifying Purity that even the Origin Singed had taken notice.
With proper Complexity, they might one day scorch even Harmonized Sourcebound Icons.
But for now...
"We may not be doomed after all," the Great Beyonder whispered.
Noah turned to her with a raised brow.
"Why do you always speak too soon—just before you're proven wrong?"
He had to ask.
Because just as the Great Beyonder finished her words...
HUUM!
Another Dead True Source blared, this one from behind Nyxal and Grys.
That brought the number to three.
And from the direction of the Wild True Source of Fear, two more Dead Source auras erupted, bringing the total to five from that side.
And it didn't stop there.
As if every Dead Thing across the merged Domus had been waiting for the perfect moment-
BZZT!
From the white halls and corridors of the Pale Verbum Labyrinth, four more Dead True Source auras surged outward in a maddened burst.
Add Yrrmoth, already advancing from that direction, and that made five from the Pale Verbum Labyrinth.
Five more from the Domus of Absolute Fear.
Three from the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality.
Twelve Dead True Sources in total.
Against the three of them.
The Great Beyonder's visage shifted—her face a mask of fury and grim realization.
She cursed under her breath.
"What a bullshit fucking move from the Wheel...merging all these Domus like this. If I finally die now after all this time because of its twisted calculations..."

sentences.text: Now was the time for him to reveal anything he had been hiding!
And perhaps reveal whatever it was that had caused the Wheel of Existence to merge multiple Gateway Domus together.
The Great Beyonder uttered those words softly, as Noah's weavings pulsed in quiet resonance.
Compared to others...what made him unique?
The answer rested entirely in his Purity.
One of his bodies, currently stationed in the True Frequency of the Singed, could feel the gaze of the Origin Singed.
And from that being's eyes, he felt something rare.
Caution.
Not hostility—but caution.
As if the Origin Singed could not fathom the level of Purity emanating from the True Source Noah had just obtained.
Of course, he held the True Source Atlas of Existence, among other things—but here, the Singed remained singular in its judgment.
Noah's path diverged from all others.
While they ascended through Lesser Sources, Greater Sources, Prime Sources, and eventually the revered Undeniable Telos Prime Sources, before evolving into True Source Complexity Entities—
He had walked a different road.
He didn't climb through Amalgamation.
He never cobbled together fragments.
He severed his Ordinances eighty-one times until they became Pathways.
And when he finally obtained a Source from the Pathway—it was already a True Source.
Noah's ascent was different.
Profoundly so!
Naturally, his Purity didn't match the conventional metrics explained by the Great Beyonder.
Nascent Source-Bearer Complexity Entities were known to have Average Purity, but he could feel it- his Purity far exceeded those bounds.
It felt as though his Purity belonged among Harmonized Sourcebound Icon Complexities.
So.
He decided to test it.

His Weaver of Existence Distinction analyzed the Pillars of Concordance cast by both the Great Beyonder and Veyl'Aethra—pillars that had turned their surrounding regions into extensions of their True Source.
His gaze then turned to the distant silver seas and rising waterfalls of Causality, where two Dead Things now approached.
And he spoke, softly.
"Pillar."
HUUM!
The Great Beyonder's eyes flew open, astonished as she heard the first word.
He didn't hesitate as he completed it.
"Of Concordance."
Three simple words.
But in the next breath—toward the direction from which the two Dead Things advanced...
A dazzling pillar of white-gold brilliance erupted.
It wasn't just flames.
This was a pillar of judgment.
A white-gold flaming monument that rippled across many light-years, rising and descending with seeming infinitude.
It spread the weavings of its True Source across the domain of Causality—and just in time.
The two Dead Things were approaching.
The Great Beyonder turned toward Noah, her gaze unreadable.
He didn't even need to look back before he spoke.
"The Purity of my True Source may have just surpassed the distinction between Nascent Source-Bearer and Harmonized Sourcebound Icon.
It seems... if Purity is high enough, even Average or Low Complexity can be overridden to exhibit power on par with higher-tiered beings."
He said it so casually.
The Great Beyonder and Veyl'Aethra exchanged glances.
The old man offered Noah a smile.
"It's always good to see the young ones outpacing us.
But let's not celebrate yet—this is only a portion of the Dead Things making their way here.
I still don't see how we'll survive the rest."
Yes.
Things were only beginning.
The Great Beyonder kept her sharp gaze fixed on Noah, speaking as she observed the two Dead Things surging toward the white-gold flaming domain where his Pillar of Concordance had been enacted.
"The ones approaching your True Source...
I know them well.
Nyxal, the Dreamer Beneath Withering Stars, bearer of the Dead True Source of Somnial Nihilum—a collapsed Source of dreams and imagination.
And Grys, the Archivist of Hollow Truths, with the Dead True Source of Veritas Moribundum—a fossilized Source of Truth that corrupts certainty itself.
Both are tricky little fuckers.
Will the Purity of your Source be enough against them?"
She asked a critical question, just as Nyxal and Grys entered Noah's expanded Pillar of Concordance of the Singed.
Nyxal's form was a titanic humanoid of ashen-gray flesh with five glowing eyes across his face.
Grys was a woman with an obsidian trident, her lower half a mass of writhing octopus-like tentacles.
The moment they breached Noah's domain, the white-gold flames surged wildly.
The flames latched onto the weavings of existence surrounding the two Dead Things—burning not with heat, but with the purity of eonic embers that could never be extinguished.
OOOH!
Roars of fury erupted from both beings.
Grys' corrupted Source shattered certainty in her surroundings, causing the white-gold flames to flicker in and out of reality.
Nyxal unleashed a source of endless, recursive dreams—powerful enough to trap even True Sources in endless loops, further disrupting the flames.
And yet...
They burned on.
Flickering, warping, but never fading.
They returned.
These were no ordinary flames.
They were the True Flames of the Singed, fueled by such terrifying Purity that even the Origin Singed had taken notice.
With proper Complexity, they might one day scorch even Harmonized Sourcebound Icons.
But for now...
"We may not be doomed after all," the Great Beyonder whispered.
Noah turned to her with a raised brow.
"Why do you always speak too soon—just before you're proven wrong?"
He had to ask.
Because just as the Great Beyonder finished her words...
HUUM!
Another Dead True Source blared, this one from behind Nyxal and Grys.
That brought the number to three.
And from the direction of the Wild True Source of Fear, two more Dead Source auras erupted, bringing the total to five from that side.
And it didn't stop there.
As if every Dead Thing across the merged Domus had been waiting for the perfect moment-
BZZT!
From the white halls and corridors of the Pale Verbum Labyrinth, four more Dead True Source auras surged outward in a maddened burst.
Add Yrrmoth, already advancing from that direction, and that made five from the Pale Verbum Labyrinth.
Five more from the Domus of Absolute Fear.
Three from the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality.
Twelve Dead True Sources in total.
Against the three of them.
The Great Beyonder's visage shifted—her face a mask of fury and grim realization.
She cursed under her breath.
"What a bullshit fucking move from the Wheel...merging all these Domus like this.
If I finally die now after all this time because of its twisted calculations..."

chapters.title: Chapter 3658 A Flame That Purifies!
paragraphs: The Great Beyonder cursed under her breath at the Wheel's calculations.
How were the three of them supposed to withstand the assault of twelve Dead True Sources of Existence?
Each one held its own complex weavings- and in that moment, Veyl'Aethra sighed, his eyes brimming with emotions far too tangled to describe.
He lifted his left hand, subtle and hidden from the sight of the Great Beyonder and Noah, who remained focused on the waves of Dead Things approaching.

His gaze fell upon his pale hand, where a swirling obsidian singularity bloomed in and out of existence. It made his entire limb spasm, flickering in and out of reality like a being that couldn't quite hold its place.
But his True Source pulsed silently.
He clenched his hand, stabilizing it. The Echo Distortion of Existence faded before it could be observed by the others.
He understood, at least in part, why the Wheel had merged the Gateway Domus together.
But he... couldn't bring himself to speak of it. Not yet.
Instead, he focused forward—preparing to unleash even more Pillars of Concordance, his True Source ready to burn at its limits.
Meanwhile, the Great Beyonder's expression darkened.
She took in the chaos around her and spoke, more to herself than to anyone else, her voice wrapped in solemn power.
"I've done this for so long. I've defended for millions of years. I thought of leaving a total of three times. But I stayed. I remained strong. Surely...this can't be how it all ends?"
Half of her attention drifted toward Noah.
As if she were still... expectantly waiting.
Noah met her gaze with a quiet smile, a flicker of calm in the storm of despair and uncertainty.
"You'll likely be put to work a little while longer," he said softly. "So hang in there."
His words carried no grandeur- just truth.
There was no need for despair.
The Wheel of Existence wasn't finished with her yet.
Then, he closed his eyes.
Even as the Dead Things closed in from every direction, he stilled his breath and listened.
To the True Source of the Singed.
Its brightness. Its brilliance.
Its Complexity.
Its Purity.
It had been the first Source to speak to him.
Why had the Wheel done what it did?
The answer was always the same.
The Variable.
He was the variable.
And so, with his heart aligned to that truth, his flames began to hum—vibrating with sacred resonance as his voice echoed out to all present beings, living and dead.
"My flames are pure."
"My flames are scorching."
"My flames are glorious."
HUUUM!
"And my flames...are empowering."
The instant his final word rang out...
He unleashed the True Flames of the Singed.

The Pillar of Concordance of the Singed erupted in brilliance, releasing ringing waves of white-gold fire that surged outward, spiraling toward the Pillar of the Great Beyonder—inscribed with trillions of runes—and the Pillar of Veyl'Aethra, etched with the unraveling strands of time itself.
The flames touched the other Pillars...
BZZT!
...and ignited them.
The unfathomably pure white-gold fire acted as a catalyst, bonding with their constructs and causing their Pillars to blaze brighter, expand, and intensify.
The Great Beyonder and Veyl'Aethra could only look on, astonished.
A True Source...was empowering the True Sources of others?
"Is this... what the Wheel saw?"
The Great Beyonder's eyes gleamed as her own True Source of Runes surged in Complexity and Purity, even if just for a moment.
And Noah?
He stood silent, listening.
The True Source of the Singed communicated with him again, just like before, speaking of its limitless possibilities, its unseen design. Not only did it sever concepts to become a Pathway...
...it could also empower True Sources.
His flames stretched far toward the regions of the Gateway Domus, toward Yrrmoth, Nyxal, and Grys, and every other incoming Dead Source.
They came into contact with them. They touched their essence.
And in doing so.
They made a distinction.
They declared those beings as enemies.
HUUM!
Noah's weavings pulsed.
The True Severed Adaptive Power of Existence activated, marking each hostile entity as an enemy whose Complexity he now needed to match—to overcome—in the battles to come.
This was his starting point.
And his flames—those wondrous flames of the Singed—continued to break down the corrupted weavings of the Dead True Sources they touched.
They were unfathomably pure.
Now, all they needed was...
Complexity!
As Noah's flames empowered the Great Beyonder and Veyl'Aethra, as he prepared to face even more Dead Things...
One more thing demanded his focus.
There were two Mechanics of Ascension among True Sources.
The first- to clash with other Sources, growing stronger through the impact and surviving collapse.
The second- Source Devouring Evolution—the path others feared.
But it was the path he wished to walk most.
One path involved attaining a Source similar to the Wild True Source in the current Domus.
The other...was to devour the Complexity and Purity of other True Sources without undergoing Fractal Collapse.
And so, he called out in thought.

"My dear Ruination, you have given me the Affix of the Severed Extractor to understand even incompatible Sources. Now, can you give me an Affix to break down and purify understood True Sources of others—so I may devour them entirely...without fracturing my existence?"
This body- his form bound to the True Source of the Singed, had arrived in the Infinite Ravines, where he had met the Great Beyonder and encountered beings with other True Sources of Existence.
He directed his message to none other than Ruination- the Ruined Miniature Wheel of Existence within the grand Wheel itself.
One of his bodies was currently traversing Frequency to Frequency with her, gathering the final Traces of the Wheel.
This body- his form bound to the True Source of the Singed, had arrived in the Infinite Ravines, where he had met the Great Beyonder and encountered beings with other True Sources of Existence.
Another body bound to the True Source of Existence itself was now engaged in the most difficult battle of his life, stretching across frequencies of reality.
He was battling the Dead Thing known as Bob- a being so unfathomably complex, even Noah could not measure the full scope of his power.
Bob's weavings had been fractured long ago—broken while being chased by the Omnifather, after he invaded the Weavings of the Wheel.
Bob had sealed his own memories, twisted time, distorted frequency all for the reason of going with the flow of the Wheel to not be found out and treated as an enemy.
He even became a disciple of the First Watcher of the Wheelomachy in this distortion of time and reality!
He had sought out entanglements like Noah, the Great Usurper, and the Peacemaker for a purposes of obtaining what he wished, and he eventually did.
Even the Omnifather, who had been chasing him across infinite echoes, had never truly discovered Bob's identity.
He was a mess of paradox, uncertainty, and time.
And Noah could not help but look forward—to the day he would forge the True Sources of Paradox, Uncertainty, Relativity, and Chronos.
But for now...
There was Bob.
There were the Infinite Ravines.
There were the True Frequencies of the Wheel.

There was the mission to fill his last Mundi of Power with a System forged of all Three States of Existence and to finally complete the Atlas of Existence- to break free of the title of Administrator.
There was the Infiniverse Megalos.
There were his True Sources.
And there was...Ruination.
