chapters.title: Chapter 3659 The Complexity of the Dead! I
paragraphs: As Noah looked at the many areas of focus he had to pour his attention into, weavings of existence continued to unfold.

The merging of the Gateway Domus was complex and chaotic, unfolding at the same time as the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality, the Pale Verbum Labyrinth, and the Domus of Absolute Fear of Existence twisted and tore into each other- each Wild True Source striving to overpower the next in a terrifying display of supremacy.

In the midst of these terrifyingly intricate reactions and interactions, in the farthest reaches where distance was nearly impossible to measure, something stirred. From the direction of the Wild True Sources of Existence where the Dead Things emerged...
Surrounded by the Wild True Source of Fear, a Dead Thing stood with its aura entirely retracted, as though it truly were lifeless.
It was something called Vha'Nekrul, the Corpse Lattice of Memory.
A Dead Thing born of the Dead True Source known as Mnemosyne Abyssum.
A True Source that dealt in memory, and at this moment, the very memory of his existence had been forgotten by the Wild True Source around him, as though he'd never been.

He appeared as a massive chained skeleton formed of crumbling brains and eyes, wrapped in flickering neural filaments. Thoughts echoed around him like whispered screams in forgotten languages, and his presence was utterly horrific.

And yet, in that moment, those crumbling eyes and brains focused on the figure of Noah and his dazzling white-gold flames- flames that were actively empowering the Pillars of Concordance of other True Sources, making them blindingly stronger.
Stronger, to the extent that even from such an impossible distance where his own Source had been erased from memory, he could still feel the looming threat.
As he watched, his weavings trembled tumultuously, as though he had uncovered something unthinkable.
And then, this Dead Thing, Vha'Nekrul, the Corpse Lattice of Memory, turned in the opposite direction and shot away with solemn purpose.
He moved across the Wild Resource of Fear as if he knew how to escape a place that had no concept of measurable distance.
His Dead True Source pulsed, contracted, and pulsed again, flickering in and out of existence as it crossed unknowable spans in mere moments.

At the same time, he seemed to manipulate his Source, causing his memory to vanish from the grasp of time itself. One second passed and yet, at the same time, thousands of years could have flowed by. It didn't matter.

It was unfathomable and hard to explain, but the distortion of the True Source was so profound that moments after he began his trajectory, he began flickering in and out of existence, depleting the authority of his True Source by a terrifying amount to do one thing.
Escape the Wild True Source of Fear.
Escape the Infinite Ravines of the Absolute Complex True Source, an ancient place he and many other Dead Things had discovered and fed from over millions of years.

None of them had truly wanted to leave. Not even the Wild True Sources of the Gateway Domus, for even they found nourishment in devouring what they could to sustain their decaying, dying True Sources.
But this Dead Thing left anyway because it had seen something.

After leaving the Infinite Ravines, all that protected it from the ravages of the Nullvein Gravewake Folds was its own decaying Source, but that Source now pulsed like it carried a signal. And Vha'Nekrul burned even more of its authority, making terrifying jumps across incalculable distances- flickering through time, or rather, the absence of it until finally, he saw it.
A blinding, swirling mass of darkness.
And his dead eyes...were relieved.
He dove in.
BOOM!
As if crashing into a sealed vault, a dead cocoon where his weary Source could rest, Vha'Nekrul exhaled soundlessly and looked around at the Wild Dead True Source permeating this strange refuge.
He didn't linger.
He could already feel it- an aura of such ancient, terrifying power that it stirred fear in what remained of him. He floated toward it, releasing his intent like a respectful knock.
"O Veltraxis, the Smiling Empty Maw... I seek your audience. I may have discovered something that matches the signs you once spoke of."
His tone was reverent, like a junior addressing an impossibly powerful elder.
And that's exactly what this was.
A deep, ancient voice erupted from the center of this place as space distorted around it, causing Vha'Nekrul to be transported instantly into a storm-wracked region formed from a violent True Source.
At its core stood a childlike humanoid floating above an Existential Shadow that devoured nearby weavings of existence.
Its grin stretched ear to ear permanently, its eyes were pure obsidian- cold and merciless.
And its voice, when it came, was terrifying in its complexity- more than anything within the Gateway Domus of Absolute Fear, the Pale Verbum Labyrinth, or the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality.
"What did you find?"
Vha'Nekrul trembled as he replied.

"Many of us have been feeding from the Infinite Ravines of an Absolute Complex True Source for eons. I myself have done so for several million years...though I've never breached the Wheel itself. But—"
"Get to the point."
WAA!
Vha'Nekrul flinched. The monstrous being waved its hand dismissively, its obsidian gaze granting him only a few more seconds to justify his presence or be erased.
The Corpse Lattice of Memory bowed its skeletal head deeply.

"Inside a Gateway Domus, I observed an existence wielding a Living True Source capable of empowering other Living Sources and suppressing Dead True Sources. You said...if such a thing ever appeared, you wanted to be told. That it might be a sign- one of the signs that an Absolute Complex True Source powerful enough to create such a being could hold the key...to saving the countless Dead True Sources lost across the Ravages of the Nullvein Gravewake Folds."
The words hung heavy in the space between them.
Opposite him, the childlike figure's obsidian eyes pulsed with keen interest. It nodded slowly, one finger rising and tapping in Vha'Nekrul's direction.

Instantly, his body trembled as his Dead True Source of Existence felt another pervading across it, a tremendously vile and complex Source that if he ever thought of denying, everything would end for him!

His tone was reverent, like a junior addressing an impossibly powerful elder.
And that's exactly what this was.
A deep, ancient voice erupted from the center of this place as space distorted around it, causing Vha'Nekrul to be transported instantly into a storm-wracked region formed from a violent True Source.
At its core stood a childlike humanoid floating above an Existential Shadow that devoured nearby weavings of existence.
Its grin stretched ear to ear permanently, its eyes were pure obsidian- cold and merciless.
And its voice, when it came, was terrifying in its complexity- more than anything within the Gateway Domus of Absolute Fear, the Pale Verbum Labyrinth, or the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality.
"What did you find?"
Vha'Nekrul trembled as he replied.
"Many of us have been feeding from the Infinite Ravines of an Absolute Complex True Source for eons.
I myself have done so for several million years...though I've never breached the Wheel itself.
But—"
"Get to the point."
WAA!
Vha'Nekrul flinched.
The monstrous being waved its hand dismissively, its obsidian gaze granting him only a few more seconds to justify his presence or be erased.
The Corpse Lattice of Memory bowed its skeletal head deeply.
"Inside a Gateway Domus, I observed an existence wielding a Living True Source capable of empowering other Living Sources and suppressing Dead True Sources.
You said...if such a thing ever appeared, you wanted to be told.

That it might be a sign- one of the signs that an Absolute Complex True Source powerful enough to create such a being could hold the key...to saving the countless Dead True Sources lost across the Ravages of the Nullvein Gravewake Folds."
The words hung heavy in the space between them.
Opposite him, the childlike figure's obsidian eyes pulsed with keen interest.
It nodded slowly, one finger rising and tapping in Vha'Nekrul's direction.

Instantly, his body trembled as his Dead True Source of Existence felt another pervading across it, a tremendously vile and complex Source that if he ever thought of denying, everything would end for him!

chapters.title: Chapter 3660 The Complexity of the Dead! II
paragraphs: In the next breath, the memories and coordinates of the place he had just left poured from him- ripped from his control. His Dead True Source of Mnemosyne Abyssum was easily overridden, even though it stood at the Harmonized Sourcebound Icon Complexity level.
The memories were read, and rapidly at that.
Then...

"Hmm...good. There is potential in this. Here is the first part of your reward. You will also gain the privilege of joining us in an official capacity...keep working hard. Return to that Infinite Ravine and observe. I will assemble a team to confirm..."
The being- Veltraxis, the Smiling Empty Maw, spoke while tossing something toward the bowing Vha'Nekrul.
An incandescent, colorless crystal.
A crystal!
Vha'Nekrul had actually been thrown a crystal, and he caught it like it was the most treasured thing in the world, his skeletal mouth even moving as he whispered what he held.
"A Sorrowglass True Source Panacea...!"
A crystal that every Dead Thing would do anything and everything to obtain. A rare relic found only in the Nullvein Gravewake Folds.
The Nullvein Gravewake Folds.

Broken stretches of existence, nonexistence, and unreality where remnants of Dead Wheels of Existence were scattered, where Dead Things roamed endlessly, hunting for even the faintest glimmer of life. Anything truly alive hid unfathomably deep in the crevices of the Nullvein Gravewake Folds.
Only when something died did its weavings become clear.
To find an Infinite Ravine of a living Wheel of Existence? That alone was a miracle.

The Sorrowglass True Source Panaceas were incomparably rare and vital to Dead Things. They could prolong the vitality of their Dead True Sources, even elevate their Complexity without forcing them to devour every Dead and Wild True Source they encountered...and risk becoming Fractal Beings.
Sorrowglass True Source Panaceas were remnants of collapsed True Sources, final dreams, unwitnessed paradoxes, and forgotten possibilities!
They appeared in unique locations where the very identity and purpose of existence began to unravel.
The Sorrowglass Crystal glowed with a colorless hue, woven from lost purpose and fractured possibilities, the remnants of shattered wheels flickering within it.
Vha'Nekrul, the Corpse Lattice of Memory, felt his Dead True Source pulse just from holding it.
Without hesitation, he devoured it. Then, with a nod toward Veltraxis- the Smiling Empty Maw whose obsidian eyes shimmered with turbidity, he turned to leave.
He didn't overstay his welcome.
The rush he felt after consuming the Sorrowglass True Source Panacea made it all feel worth it!
But he didn't know.
He didn't know he had just acted as the bridge between forces that were never meant to be joined.
He left behind an entity of terrifying Complexity, floating amidst storms of swirling existence, who murmured quietly to himself.
"Could this one be it? I cannot bear to see another Wheel of Existence shattered and broken..."
Veltraxis spoke those words.
And yet... the permanent grin carved from ear to ear across his face made the sentiment sound eerily unfathomable. The words and the expression simply didn't match.
Across Existence.
Beyond the Infinite Ravines of a certain Absolute Complex True Source.
Inside that True Source, this grandiose Wheel of Existence...within the Frequency of Blood.

A region thick with crimson strings of existence, where the air radiated the metallic taste and scent of concentrated bloodlust and power. In this place, the figures of Noah and Ruination could be seen.
Noah floated in a stellar sea of blood, watching Ruination as she finished absorbing another crimson-gold Piece of a Spoke of the Wheel.

They had been moving through frequency after frequency, gathering more pieces of the Wheel. And with each one, her status as a Ruined Miniare Wheel of Existence grew- her Complexity rising to terrifying heights.

Noah watched her closely as he had already discussed with her what he needed. A methodology- an Affix! One that could purify Wild and Dead True Sources of Existence. A way for him to use Source Devouring Evolution...without triggering a Fractal Collapse of Existence.
Without becoming a Fractal Being.
After he proposed the task, the most important thing wasn't what she said.
It was what she didn't say.
She didn't say that it was impossible!
Instead, she turned contemplative. And after a few long moments, her wide crimson-gold eyes lifted to meet his.

"I'll have to abandon all other potential Affix plans except Burnt Weaver and Severed Extractor. At my current stage, I believe I can support a new Affix- one capable of purifying Wild and Dead True Sources of Existence. But it would demand nearly all of my Complexity. My Complexity, which is now..."
She raised her hands and looked at herself.
Noah studied her, too. His weavings told him she was truly evolving and becoming something more.
Something dangerously close to a Wheel of Existence.
A wholly unique construct.
And so, he nodded.
"You can proceed with forging it...if it's currently viable."
Ruination received the command and stepped forward, her hands resting gently against his chest as though she were touching the pristine True Source Atlas of Existence hidden underneath itself.
Her eyes shimmered with reverence. Crimson-gold light surged from her body as she began to forge a terrifying Affix.
"I'll call this type of Affix...the Affix of the Ruined Miniare Wheel."
She paused, searching for the right name. The name that would match the sacred, terrifying construct she was about to weave into her master's very existence.
"It shall be named...the Affix of the Cradle of Purity."
The Cradle of Purity.
BOOM!
The Ruined Miniare Wheel of Existence began etching a terrifying wonder into Noah's weavings. He watched her quietly, his thoughts drifting even as she worked.
Her path seemed clear now. She would continue scouring the frequencies, gathering more Traces and Spokes of the Wheel.
But one question loomed.
A question that buzzed within Noah, and would haunt anyone who looked just a little deeper.
A question about the Wheel itself.
Because anything that had fragments of its whole scattered across creation, pieces, traces, even segments of its spokes...meant one thing.
The whole...was broken.
Or shattered.
So if there were multiple fragments of the Wheel across countless frequencies, what did that say about the Wheel of Existence itself?

chapters.title: Chapter 3661 The Complexity of the Living I
paragraphs: Was the Wheel of Existence still whole, or had it shattered, yet somehow remained capable of expressing its power as a living, Absolute Complex True Source?
Or was Noah missing something critical? Just because its pieces stretched across countless frequencies didn't necessarily mean it had shattered and scattered throughout existence.
These thoughts permeated his consciousness, lingering deep within even as the presence of Ruination flickered in and out beside him.
Ruination.

Her hand pressed against his chest, her fingers carving into him as they began altering something intrinsic, something that felt like a part of existence itself. He could feel her gaze, piercing into him as if she were looking cor something. He smiled at that. What could this girl possibly hope to find?
Ruination.
That was her name, and her identity. Even now, she remembered who she was. The treasure of taboo- the weapon that once brought ruin in the hands of the Sages of the Dark Universe.
She remembered the man before her. How, piece by piece, he had gathered her shattered self and made her whole. That felt like eons ago!
She remembered every single thing he'd done since. And during all that time, she had done everything in her power to be useful to him.
Because she saw it- the terrifying weight he carried on his shoulders. A burden no other existence should ever have to bear.
There were moments she had helped him. And more recently, she'd reached a state of being that allowed her to lessen the crushing weight bearing down on her master.
The distinction of a Wheel.
A Ruined Miniare Wheel of Existence.
A Wheel was a Wheel, no matter its state. And Ruination had found her purpose. She knew exactly where she needed to go and how to give back to the man who had given her everything.
Her very existence was shifting, evolving, and still, she remained irrevocably tied to him. Tied to the very concept of Ruination, and yet he had elevated her core concept into something far more.
Ruination itself had been made a Pathway to the True Source.
And that meant Ruination herself...was walking the path to becoming a True Source.
And yet...wasn't she already a type of Wheel?
Didn't that mean that she should already be a type of True Source?

The wonder of such a reality pulsed through her. She didn't tell him how close she was- not yet. She wanted it to be a surprise. He was stretching himself thin, doing countless things across existence as this was something she could bring him.
Something only she could give.
Because as she consumed more and more fragments of the Wheel, as her signature as a Wheel of Existence grew stronger, and so too did the reality that she was becoming a True Source.
Her hand cradled his chest, and she felt the boundless weavings of the True Source Atlas of Existence beneath her fingers. She closed her eyes.
In her musings, she finished etching the third Affix she was working on- meant to aid her Master and to ease his burdens even just a little.
The Cradle of Purity.
An Affix of the Ruined Miniare Wheel of Existence.

Ruination had poured everything into it. From the memories she had seen within her Master regarding the Infinite Ravines he carried in his mind—she had taken every last ounce of her ruined power and woven it into this Affix.
And still, she felt like it wasn't enough.
Opening her mouth, she finally spoke, her voice soft.

"The Affix of the Cradle of Purity is designed to take in Wild, Dead, and Living True Sources of existence and break them down into something pure and viable. It separates the corruption and taint of the complexity of True Sources by refining and breaking them down. To make that possible, as much as fifty percent of the targeted weavings will be lost. But what remains will be the pure, filtered essence of existence, known as Pure Natal True Source Weavings of Existence."

The moment the terrifying words left her lips, she felt a knot of frustration as if it should have been more. The Cradle of Purity should have been capable of refining one hundred percent of the weavings...of turning them all into Pure Natal Weavings!
But she knew that Existence had its limits.
And she was still limited as her current power couldn't bend Existence that far. Not yet.
So even as a storm of crimson and gold raged around them, she finished carving a massive rune into his chest and branding him with yet another Affix. It resembled a fantastical cradle.
A celestial construct meant to receive Wild, Dead, and Living True Sources and refine them into something not just consumable by her Master...but something he could choose to share with others.
Though she would much prefer he keep it for himself.
Still...she knew who he was.
She knew that in the near future, some of the gifts that came from the Cradle of Purity would inevitably be given to a few others because her Master never stopped giving.
And at times she wanted him to take everything for himself without worry.
She lifted her hand from his chest, lost in thought, until she felt his presence glowing and warm, near hers. He tilted her chin up with his hand and smiled.

"You've just casually done something that multiple True Sources of existence haven't achieved in millions of years. And yet, why do you look disappointed? You just created a way to devour other True Sources without becoming a Fractal Being. You know that, right?"
His words pulsed with brilliance, as if trying to remind her that what she had done was no small feat.
But Ruination shook her head as she responded:
"Just give me more time, Master. I'll make the Cradle of Purity everything it's meant to be and more."
She'd set the bar high for herself. What she wanted to create went far beyond this.
Her Master understood. He nodded, his voice low and commanding as he rose to his feet, shaking his head with a soft laugh.
"You have all the time in the world. Come on, let's get you more pieces of the Wheel- whether it's whole or shattered."
HUUM!
His weavings buzzed.
And just like that, he moved forward once more.
For her.
Always for others.
And as he did, Ruination's resolve hardened even further.
A True Source was just the beginning.
She would give him so much more!

chapters.title: Chapter 3662 The Complexity of the Living II
paragraphs: As she moved with her Master from the Frequency of Blood as Ruination had obtained all the hidden pieces and spokes of the Wheel buried within that realm.
Another part of her body remained within the Infiniverse Megalos.
The ever-changing construct she'd been competing with and losing to, countless times in terms of utility and advancement over the months.
But still, they were together.
At this moment, a crimson-gold figure of Ruination floated into a small world nestled within the heart of the Infiniverse Vein.
A world where floating islands dangled in the skies like ornaments.

The ground was blanketed in sheets of snow, while the fantastical islands above spilled cascading waterfalls, each one formed from severed concepts of Dreams, Avalon, Genesis, Helios, Quantum, Prana, and many others—each unique, each vibrant in its own way.
This was a world mirrored after the Beast World, the one their Master had delved into from his original blue planet.
The same world where he had claimed a spiritual land that had evolved into the terrifying thing now known as the Infiniverse Megalos.

Amidst the many floating islands, Ruination drifted toward a simple one- a quiet island that resembled that spiritual land exactly. The same land where her Master had fought against a certain prideful penguin and other spiritual beasts to gain ownership.
Upon this island, a woman draped in white sat in a snowy field.
Her eyes shimmered like starlight—pupils swirling with countless layers of Megalos themselves.
Ruination appeared behind the Infiniverse Megalos Body, her voice calm as her feet touched down upon the snow.
"Master is battling a psychotic Dead Thing across realities. Another part of him is stepping into the Ravines, about to face even more Dead Things, and we...we sit here."
We sit here.
She felt ashamed just saying the words aloud.
The Infiniverse Megalos Body didn't even turn as she replied.
"You did a decent enough job creating that Cradle of Purity just now. You're doing something."
A decent enough job.
That's what she said about a construct designed to do what hadn't been done for eons.
A construct that allowed True Sources to be purified and absorbed without risking Fractal Collapse of Existence!
And still...she called it a decent job.
Ruination somehow agreed and nodded.
"What are you doing?" she asked softly.
How were they contributing?
While their Master bore the weight of countless realities—fighting, building, and protecting, what were they doing?
The stellar eyes of the Infiniverse Megalos Body blinked slowly. She continued gazing at the endless fields of snow, her fair fingers playing in the frost as she answered.
"You are becoming a Ruined Miniare Wheel of Existence. I am trying to become an Absolute Complex True Source of Existence."
BOOM!
Shocking words left her lips—but she continued casually, as if discussing the weather.

"I've looked at all the avenues and possibilities. With the Singed taken to the level of a True Source, I already have the flame of a Source burning within the heart of the Infiniverse Megalos. It can serve as the fuel for a Wheel of Existence. But I need something more. Something grander. The words of that Dead Thing...they've been echoing in my mind."
The words of a Dead Thing?
Ruination raised a brow, then settled beside the Infiniverse Megalos Body in the snow.
"The psychotic Bob? What part of his words could possibly cause someone to reflect?"
She didn't like the time and energy her Master had to spend on that Dead Thing.
But the Megalos replied evenly:

"That which Innervates the Wheels of Existence. I don't know what it is. I don't even know if it exists. But maybe that's what I need before I step forward to become an Absolute Complex True Source. Or...I brute-force it. I devour all the possibilities and frequencies of this Wheel of Existence and take everything it has."
WAA!
Her eyes gleamed with a chilling brilliance.
Ruination didn't reply.
She simply raised her head, watching as thousands of snowflakes began to drift around them on this floating island.
Two terrifying treasures sat side by side.
One—already a form of a Wheel of Existence.
The other...something far more unfathomable.
Both of them were thinking the same terrifying thing—how to become something greater. Something worthy of a single man.
The True Severed Origin Osmontian!
At some point, in the stillness of the snow, the Infiniverse Megalos Body finally turned toward her.
"My path is harder. Yours is more straightforward. I've gone ahead and used the Source of that Queen of Matter. I'm expanding into more and more frequencies of the Wheel.

I've begun spreading my weavings across them—gathering every Piece and Trace of the Wheel for you. It should accelerate your progression... so you can become a more complete Wheel for Master to wield."
She spoke about something terrifying—as if she were describing how she'd brewed tea or prepared a meal for their Master.
And yet, she was manipulating a Source so rare, it had once only existed to observe fables within the states of Matter.
Now, she was spreading her will across frequencies with it and taking exactly what she wanted.
Ruination raised a brow, then nodded, adding with a light shrug.
"Keep that Queen of Matter away from Master, if you can. She seems like another brand of crazy that might distract him more than others."
She remembered the woman's eyes—those mad, elated eyes when she had grabbed her throat. As if she enjoyed being choked.
Her Master didn't need that kind of chaos in his life.
But the Infiniverse Megalos Body shook her head and replied calmly:

"Women and food are some of the few...weavings of Existence that Master still enjoys in these craziness of Existence. Food is just a hobby for his palate. Women, though... he complements them and they complement him. They help him stay sane. Even if he added a hundred more, I wouldn't be averse to it.

And that Queen of Matter? She's like us. She adores Master. Don't let her eccentricities bother you. Focus on yourself—and leave the rest to me. When you're ready for the Pieces and Traces of the Wheel I'm gathering... just say the word as they might be enough to complete you."
Her gaze shifted onto Ruination as she continued.
"How close are you to attaining your True Source?"
Like an older sister offering advice to her younger sibling, the Infiniverse Megalos asked gently, powerfully, and with all the weight of power behind her words!

sentences.text: As she moved with her Master from the Frequency of Blood as Ruination had obtained all the hidden pieces and spokes of the Wheel buried within that realm.
Another part of her body remained within the Infiniverse Megalos.
The ever-changing construct she'd been competing with and losing to, countless times in terms of utility and advancement over the months.
But still, they were together.
At this moment, a crimson-gold figure of Ruination floated into a small world nestled within the heart of the Infiniverse Vein.
A world where floating islands dangled in the skies like ornaments.

The ground was blanketed in sheets of snow, while the fantastical islands above spilled cascading waterfalls, each one formed from severed concepts of Dreams, Avalon, Genesis, Helios, Quantum, Prana, and many others—each unique, each vibrant in its own way.
This was a world mirrored after the Beast World, the one their Master had delved into from his original blue planet.
The same world where he had claimed a spiritual land that had evolved into the terrifying thing now known as the Infiniverse Megalos.
Amidst the many floating islands, Ruination drifted toward a simple one- a quiet island that resembled that spiritual land exactly.
The same land where her Master had fought against a certain prideful penguin and other spiritual beasts to gain ownership.
Upon this island, a woman draped in white sat in a snowy field.
Her eyes shimmered like starlight—pupils swirling with countless layers of Megalos themselves.
Ruination appeared behind the Infiniverse Megalos Body, her voice calm as her feet touched down upon the snow.
"Master is battling a psychotic Dead Thing across realities.
Another part of him is stepping into the Ravines, about to face even more Dead Things, and we...we sit here."
We sit here.
She felt ashamed just saying the words aloud.
The Infiniverse Megalos Body didn't even turn as she replied.
"You did a decent enough job creating that Cradle of Purity just now.
You're doing something."
A decent enough job.
That's what she said about a construct designed to do what hadn't been done for eons.
A construct that allowed True Sources to be purified and absorbed without risking Fractal Collapse of Existence!
And still...she called it a decent job.
Ruination somehow agreed and nodded.
"What are you doing?" she asked softly.
How were they contributing?
While their Master bore the weight of countless realities—fighting, building, and protecting, what were they doing?
The stellar eyes of the Infiniverse Megalos Body blinked slowly.
She continued gazing at the endless fields of snow, her fair fingers playing in the frost as she answered.
"You are becoming a Ruined Miniare Wheel of Existence.
I am trying to become an Absolute Complex True Source of Existence."
BOOM!
Shocking words left her lips—but she continued casually, as if discussing the weather.
"I've looked at all the avenues and possibilities.
With the Singed taken to the level of a True Source, I already have the flame of a Source burning within the heart of the Infiniverse Megalos.
It can serve as the fuel for a Wheel of Existence.
But I need something more.
Something grander.
The words of that Dead Thing...they've been echoing in my mind."
The words of a Dead Thing?
Ruination raised a brow, then settled beside the Infiniverse Megalos Body in the snow.
"The psychotic Bob?
What part of his words could possibly cause someone to reflect?"
She didn't like the time and energy her Master had to spend on that Dead Thing.
But the Megalos replied evenly:
"That which Innervates the Wheels of Existence.
I don't know what it is.
I don't even know if it exists.
But maybe that's what I need before I step forward to become an Absolute Complex True Source.
Or...I brute-force it.
I devour all the possibilities and frequencies of this Wheel of Existence and take everything it has."
WAA!
Her eyes gleamed with a chilling brilliance.
Ruination didn't reply.
She simply raised her head, watching as thousands of snowflakes began to drift around them on this floating island.
Two terrifying treasures sat side by side.
One—already a form of a Wheel of Existence.
The other...something far more unfathomable.
Both of them were thinking the same terrifying thing—how to become something greater.
Something worthy of a single man.
The True Severed Origin Osmontian!
At some point, in the stillness of the snow, the Infiniverse Megalos Body finally turned toward her.
"My path is harder.
Yours is more straightforward.
I've gone ahead and used the Source of that Queen of Matter.
I'm expanding into more and more frequencies of the Wheel.
I've begun spreading my weavings across them—gathering every Piece and Trace of the Wheel for you.
It should accelerate your progression... so you can become a more complete Wheel for Master to wield."
She spoke about something terrifying—as if she were describing how she'd brewed tea or prepared a meal for their Master.
And yet, she was manipulating a Source so rare, it had once only existed to observe fables within the states of Matter.
Now, she was spreading her will across frequencies with it and taking exactly what she wanted.
Ruination raised a brow, then nodded, adding with a light shrug.
"Keep that Queen of Matter away from Master, if you can.
She seems like another brand of crazy that might distract him more than others."
She remembered the woman's eyes—those mad, elated eyes when she had grabbed her throat.
As if she enjoyed being choked.
Her Master didn't need that kind of chaos in his life.
But the Infiniverse Megalos Body shook her head and replied calmly:
"Women and food are some of the few...weavings of Existence that Master still enjoys in these craziness of Existence.
Food is just a hobby for his palate.
Women, though... he complements them and they complement him.
They help him stay sane.
Even if he added a hundred more, I wouldn't be averse to it.
And that Queen of Matter?
She's like us.
She adores Master.
Don't let her eccentricities bother you.
Focus on yourself—and leave the rest to me.
When you're ready for the Pieces and Traces of the Wheel I'm gathering... just say the word as they might be enough to complete you."
Her gaze shifted onto Ruination as she continued.

Like an older sister offering advice to her younger sibling, the Infiniverse Megalos asked gently, powerfully, and with all the weight of power behind her words!

chapters.title: Chapter 3663 The Complexity of the Living III
paragraphs: How far was Ruination from achieving the True Source of Ruination?
Such a heavy question hung in the air as two women sat in a field of snow, atop a floating island within a world nestled inside a massive Infiniverse Vein.
Ruination answered simply.
"Soon. But that's my surprise for Master. Do you have anything?"
She asked with flashing, competitive eyes.
At that moment, the figure of the Infiniverse Megalos Body rose, her stellar eyes fixed on the snowstorm that had begun to intensify over the once-tranquil land.

"The purity of the Flame of the Singed burning within me has allowed me to begin converting my vibrant complexity into refined weavings-ones nearly identical in quality to what the Affix of the Cradle of Purity can provide. I've already started collecting these weavings, and I can direct them toward the foundational Pillars of the Infiniverse Megalos to become a True Source. If you don't hurry, it might be me who gifts Master a True Source within the next hour."
BOOM!
Her words were outrageous.
Ruination stood too with a spark of seriousness in her expression.
"I... will take those Pieces and Traces of the Wheel you've gathered so far starting now."
She said it with a fire in her voice.

The Infiniverse Megalos Body smiled lightly, then waved her hand—and in an instant, the snowy skies ruptured. From above, dazzling Pieces and Spokes of the Wheel, drawn from multiple Frequencies, began gushing down.
Ruination leapt skyward to collect them all.
She felt as if she were racing against time.
Elsewhere, within the vast Infiniverse Vein.
Noah sat on the edge of a farm.
Wind whipped his dark hair as he looked out over acres of thriving land, clothed in simple, loose-fitting white garments that revealed his sculpted form.

All around him, countless fields shimmered with potent Waves of Existence, their crops nourished by the blood of Pioneers and Source Entities he'd once discovered within the lands of Hell Terra Firma.
But he had evolved so far... that these weavings could no longer impact him much.
His thoughts briefly drifted to Hell Terra Firma, where his satellites still roamed, seeking any lingering secrets in that mysterious land devoid of Authority.
If the Primal Flame of the Wheel had been hidden there, what else could be?
It was just a passing thought in his mind.
He raised his head, sensing the connections of Ruination and the Infiniverse Megalos as he could distinctly feel they were up to something.
But he let them be as he looked out around him.
It felt almost strange, his main body sitting calmly in a farm, while other aspects of him battled Dead Things across Frequencies or explored the Infinite Ravines.
He was stretched across the cosmos, yet somehow still grounded- always right here.
Within the protective folds of the Infiniverse Megalos.
And now, he was about to embark on another fantastical endeavor within this land he called home.
He looked down at his chest—at the True Source Atlas of Existence embedded within him. His gaze landed on the last remaining empty Mundi of Power, and he murmured.
"Let's go ahead and complete the Atlas, why don't we?"
HUUM!
With the quiet command of his voice, the wheel-like Atlas began to hum and vibrate. In its final Mundi, wondrous particles began to bloom.
Noah didn't yet know what kind of System of Existence would emerge...
But he was only just laying its foundation.
And the foundation would be grand.
"Since the last system embraced Dark Matter and Anti-Matter... this final one will include all three states of existence."
WAA!
The foundation sparked to life in spectacular fashion.
In another Mundi of Power, he felt the Pathway to the Source of Ingeniare activate—buzzing with brilliance.
He raised a brow.
"Oh?"
It whispered to him—ideas, designs.
Why not do what others never could?
It spoke of the Domus of Pale Verbum Labyrinth, Absolute Fear of Existence, and the Hollow Cascade of Reversed Causality.
Could a new System of Existence be forged- one built upon Verbum, Fear, and Causality?

If so, could it birth a True Source that allowed him to devour Wild True Sources as easily as that rare being the Great Beyonder once mentioned—one whose nature matched the very Wild True Source he was currently immersed in?
The idea hovered briefly in Noah's mind.
Then he nodded.
Let's see where it leads.
And so, the final System of Existence for his Atlas began.
Right there, with his main body, in the middle of a farm.
The same farm he had once dreamed of retiring in, but retirement would have to wait.
Because nothing was ever so simple.
Not when the memories of Bob delivered by the hands of the Great Usurper spoke of even more complex threats lurking beyond the Infinite Ravines of the Wheel of Existence.
There was an entity that had annihilated the initial weavings of the Wheel Bob came from.
Now, that being was seeking the same thing Bob himself was after.
If such a being existed—was it truly alone?
Were there others like it?
And if becoming a True Source was only the beginning, as the Great Beyonder warned... then Noah would have to postpone his peaceful farm life indefinitely.
But...
"I like it."
WAA!
He loved the journey.
He had loved the fantastical weavings of existence ever since the first day he summoned a fireball into his hand.
He knew the future wouldn't be easy.
There would be catastrophes.
There would be enemies that might even push him to fury.
And then...there were the words of Ashmole.
The dead Wandering Alchemist had told him that across Existence, there will always be Oddities who defy all logic—who are utterly ridiculous in every way.
Ashmole stayed that he could not wait for the day when one of them—someone even more absurd than Noah came to face him.
To suffocate him. To overwhelm him. So that he could finally know what it feels like.
Noah chuckled.
Because that's exactly why he moved the way he did.
So that day would never come.
So that no existence would ever outmatch or outpace him.
And that's why...
"Cheats. Quintessence. Paradox...you all need to get a move on."
He whispered to the unique Pathways within him—urging them toward True Source Ascension.
So that he could remain...
A monster.
A breaker of rules.
A defier of the boundless weavings of complexity.
Because he...
He was just getting started!

chapters.title: Chapter 3664 The Complexity of the Living IV
paragraphs: He was simply getting started!

And so, he focused inward—while the last and final System of Existence was being forged in the Ninth Mundi of Power, his attention remained locked on the current battle that spanned across Frequencies.
The battle against the Dead Thing, Bob!
Inside the Frequency of Mana.
A blue slime floated in an endless, azure sea of pure energy, humming to itself as its bright, circular eyes scanned the surroundings. It noticed clusters of other slimes drifting nearby.
Straightening up, it aimed to approach a group of elegant female slimes to show off the purity of its mana when, all of a sudden...
BOOM...CRACK!
The once-stable waves of mana surrounding it exploded and shattered in a horrifying cascade, as if existence itself were being erased.
Everything nearby faced decimation and collapse. The blue slime found itself fragmenting into countless shards, its weavings of existence on the verge of dispersing entirely.
Just as it was about to perish, it saw them- the ones responsible.

A tentacled entity with a bald, round head glowed with purple and black light. Opposite him stood a humanoid being shimmering with stellar black brilliance. Behind him, obsidian halos spun, and wings of starlit shadow unfurled in full.
The halos above his head spun violently and gushed forth a terrifying weaving of existence. The breakdown and collapse that had stretched across light-years in the surrounding regions...
Began to reverse.
The blue slime felt its shattered weavings reform, slowly returning to what they once were. The cracks that splintered reality began to mend.
And in just a brief moment—
SAA!
Everything was back to normal.
The blue slime and countless other beings in the region glanced around in shock, their trembling eyes darting nervously. And then, the bold little slime screamed first.
"What the fuck was that?!"
They had all felt the collapse of their very existence—only to have it restored. But the ones responsible?
Gone.
They had already disappeared into the Weave, shattering one plane of reality to reappear in another Frequency entirely.
BOOM!
Every impact was existence-shattering. The terrifying True Source of Khaos only seemed to grow stronger and more unhinged with every passing second.
It was as if Bob was regaining the fullness of his power with each beat, each breath—moving closer and closer to becoming a more complete Harmonized Sourcebound Icon.

Existence fractured faster with each clash. Noah had to keep pace, releasing his own True Source of Existence, letting it proliferate through the Frequencies, mending what was broken and restoring what once was.
The battle was a stalemate. Despite the raw power of Khaos, Noah's existence was actively adapting. With every passing moment, his complexity increased.
Bob saw this. He shook his head, and then after what felt like ages, spoke once again.

"None of this is needed. None of this has to happen. Even now, I've kept the weavings of the two Wheels behind me mostly dormant. I don't want to taint anything. All I need... is entry into a True Frequency. You could end all of this peacefully, my friend."
BOOM!
Their weavings clashed again. Existence cracked, twisted, distorted—and then reformed—as they plunged into the dark embrace of the Weave once more.
Noah didn't relent. His True Source of Existence permeated the space, spreading outward to overwhelm and collapse every remnant of Khaos it encountered.
But as he did this, he replied to Bob with vibrant waves of tyranny surging around him.
"Have you heard the fable of the Scorpion and the Frog?"
Bob blinked, clearly caught off guard. He looked at Noah, trying to determine if he'd heard him correctly, then shook his head.
He had never heard such a ridiculous tale.

Even as their True Sources continued to collide—distorting reality with each strike—Noah pressed on, his eyes radiating with cosmic brilliance that made him look like an ancient titan of stellar obsidian brilliance!
"A Scorpion and a Frog met on the banks of a raging river. It was too treacherous for the Scorpion to cross, so he politely asked the Frog to carry him across. Do you know what the Frog did?"
Noah asked it casually. And when Bob heard the direction the story was going, a flash of anger crossed his face. Khaos around him began to bubble with seething intensity.
Still, Noah continued.

"The Frog was suspicious as fuck. He said, 'How do I know you won't sting me?' And the Scorpion replied—completely rationally—'Because if I sting you, we'll both drown.' It made sense. The Frog hesitated but eventually agreed, letting the Scorpion ride on his back as he began to cross the river."
Noah's voice dropped.

"But halfway across... the Scorpion struck. It stung the Frog, poisoning him. As they began to sink, the dying Frog asked, 'Why the fuck would you do that? Now we're both going to die!' And the Scorpion replied..."
He paused in the eye of the storm, his voice calm amidst the crashing chaos.
"'It's in my nature.'"
Bob's expression soured. He didn't answer, only glanced behind him—toward the two massive Wheels, black and white, as though grappling with a difficult decision.
Noah didn't stop.
"So what lesson do you take from that? Because to me—you're the Scorpion. Even if it kills you. Even if it destroys everything—you'll still sting. That is just your nature."
He exhaled sharply.
"So no. I won't carry you across the river. I won't take you to a True Frequency of Existence."
His tone darkened.
"I'll learn more about you instead. Because ever since arriving in the Infinite Ravines... things about your nature are starting to become clearer."
BOOM!
Another clash. Their weavings collided, and the scenery shifted.
They now stood within the Frequency of Night.
Endless starlight stretched across a cosmic void.
In that moment, Bob's weaving hesitated.
"...What did you say?"
He hadn't cared much about the Scorpion and the Frog.
But now—at the mention of something else—his eyes narrowed with cold calculation. His voice dropped, cautious.
"The Infinite Ravines? You arrived in the Infinite Ravines?!"

Because ever since arriving in the Infinite Ravines... things about your nature are starting to become clearer."
BOOM!
Another clash.
Their weavings collided, and the scenery shifted.
They now stood within the Frequency of Night.
Endless starlight stretched across a cosmic void.
In that moment, Bob's weaving hesitated.
"...What did you say?"
He hadn't cared much about the Scorpion and the Frog.
But now—at the mention of something else—his eyes narrowed with cold calculation.
His voice dropped, cautious.
"The Infinite Ravines?
You arrived in the Infinite Ravines?!"

chapters.title: Chapter 3665 The Complexity of the Living V
paragraphs: The way Bob asked the question made it clear—something that should never have been done, had been done. His gaze locked onto Noah with a stern intensity as he sought confirmation.
"You sent a part of yourself to the Infinite Ravines?!"
He asked again, as if needing to hear it aloud.
Noah met the being's stare calmly. His silence served as a direct answer.
Bob shook his head slowly, as though the knowledge itself was a curse.

"You... haha, fuck. I told you—every Wheel of Existence has its most unique entities. And you? You're like a fucking beacon. You shine too bright, too strange. In a place like the Infinite Ravines, where Dead Things roam... your mere presence draws them in. If even one of them catches a glimpse of you—senses the difference—they'll spread word. And then you'll face an onslaught of Dead Things, all desperate for that. The same thing I'm after."
Bob's words came in a rush, tumbling one after another as his frustration mounted.
Noah considered them carefully. This wasn't something he dismissed easily. Coldly, he asked.
"My presence alone in the Infinite Ravines could cause such an avalanche?"
Bob nodded, then reached out behind him.
The illusory white Wheel began to stir, moving closer, floating toward him until it hovered at his fingertips.

"Your presence... is not just your presence. The Dead Things in the Ravines—wandering the unknown Nullvein Gravewake Folds of collapsed Wheels—they seek sustenance from Wild True Sources. Yes. But they also search for differences. For anything new. Any anomaly."
A new term appeared for Noah.
Nullvein Gravewake Folds of collapsed Wheels and existence. These were the endless regions that stood outside of Infinite Ravines of Absolute Complex True Sources?
Bob paused, his voice growing graver with each word as he continued.

"Because when they sense difference... it might mean the Wheel that the Infinite Ravines are connected to holds something more. Something unique. THAT. A pathway. A gateway. Whether it's true or not doesn't matter. If one of them suspects it, others will come. They'll come to confirm. And when they arrive, your very being will only solidify their suspicions as when I looked at you, I also became more certain that this Wheel might truly hold a great piece of a puzzle! And that's when things will spiral. Beings like me—or worse—will come. Man..."
He exhaled deeply, as if dreading what must come next.
"I never wanted things to reach this point."
But he believed they had.
"It means I'll have to get serious now—get what I need before chaos spreads. I... didn't want to do this, Osmont. I didn't want to do this."

There was desperation in his eyes as, without warning, the illusory White Wheel was suddenly in his grasp. Complexity surged around him, while Noah's True Source of Existence crashed down in raging waves.

Bob's state of Khaos elevated his power even further, yet the chaos dispersed anything near him. And in his hands, the white Wheel radiated a strange, eerie splendor—its glow pierced with the screams of countless beings.
And Bob—he did the unthinkable.
"OOOH!"
He began to pull the Wheel apart.
He was breaking it.
Tears welled in his eyes.
At the same time, Noah's weavings received a transmission from the Great Usurper—an echo of shock and revelation.

|He's burning them... no, he's burning half of all the lifeforms within the White Wheel of Existence! And he's doing it in a way that purges even the ones I had overtaken! He's breaking the White Wheel of Existence!|
WAA!
Bob was breaking the Wheel.

And he did so with a terrible sorrow etched into his face, using Khaos as a shield against Noah's furious attacks. But then—without warning—a dazzling, stellar obsidian Pillar of Concordance erupted above him.
Brilliant.
Stellar.
Obsidian.
It pierced through the violet Khaos like a blade through silk, crashing into Bob. The obsidian light struck his skin, slamming into his bald head—half of the Pillar's brilliance shattered on contact.
But—
"I didn't want to do this!"
Bob roared with anguish, even as fracture lines began to crawl across the surface of the White Wheel. In the next moment, Primal Flames—drawn from Hell Terra Firma—erupted around him.
He was burning it all.
Even as Noah's True Source bore down on him, disintegrating the top half of his head, Bob continued!
His face was twisted—not with fury—but with mad sorrow.
He screamed.
"Break!"
A shattering.
Bob...was breaking a Wheel of Existence.
BOOOM!
The dazzling White Wheel split in half. At its fracture point, the Primal Flames surged outward—releasing potent, unfamiliar waves of energy.
Unlike anything Noah had ever seen.
The energy was too pristine.
Too unfathomable.
And Bob—he harnessed all of it. He wrapped it in the flames and didn't hurl it at Noah. No—he directed it upward.
Reality itself tore open.
Existence buckled and screamed as the Weave split and warped. The force of the Wheel's destruction wasn't meant for annihilation.
It was meant for entry.
Guided by the Primal Flames, the force surged toward a distant shimmer of white-gold light.
The flames of the Singed.
But not from the Frequency of Flames.
No.
These were the True Flames.
Of the True Frequency of the Singed.
And when Bob confirmed it...
"OOOH!"

He completely tore the White Wheel in two, using its force to rip open a massive rift above. It was a wound in existence itself. But from it... spilled the impossible. True Flames—of a True Frequency.

With the shattered Wheel in each hand, Bob howled in despair. More than half his head was gone, along with huge portions of his complexity. Yet he soared toward the wound he had carved into reality—across the path of chaos and flame.
Noah roared in rage, his Pillar of Concordance chasing behind him. He saw Bob engulfed in the True Flames of the Singed, assaulted from every direction.
Yet...
Bob raised his left hand.
He burned the broken half of the White Wheel in his grip—sacrificing it to shield himself from annihilation.
And with that act—after the unthinkable destruction of one of the Dead Absolute Complex True Sources of Existence...
Bob crossed the threshold.
And entered a True Frequency.

chapters.title: Chapter 3666 Ashes I
paragraphs: The True Frequency of the Singed.
Inside it, Noah remained atop the blistering True Heart of Existence.

The same True Heart of Existence that was considered the Source of the scattered Flames of the Wheel of Existence—and only a fraction of what made up the Absolute Complex True Source that was the Wheel of Existence.

Its gloriously pure white flames and blood continued to surge into his body as he sought to harness that unparalleled purity to elevate his other pathways, testing if they, too, could ascend to the level of True Sources.
The effectiveness had dropped significantly after he attained the True Source of the Singed, yet he remained here nonetheless as he did not stop.

He could feel the distant gaze of the Origin Singed. And at that moment, his expression shifted—eyes narrowing as he turned toward a distant region within the vast True Frequency of the Wheel. There, the brilliant white-gold space split apart and tore open as a shattered white Wheel of Existence pierced through, and it was carrying none other than...
Bob.
BOOM!
He crashed into the True Frequency of the Singed, having done the impossible.
He had shattered an Absolute Complex True Source—even if it had already been dead, just to brute force his way into a True Frequency of Existence.

Noah's body, still draining the purity of the True Heart of Existence, now only contained the residual power of the True Source of the Singed. At most, he could express a fraction of its might through his form here.
But even that, magnified by the effects of the System of Existence of Ordo Ab Chao—wasn't enough to stop Bob.
And now, Bob was in a True Frequency of the Wheel, exactly where he wanted to be!

The moment he arrived, tears spilled from his eyes—eyes that shone like boundless singularities. Behind him, the other body of Noah followed, trailing an obsidian Pillar of Concordance and spinning halos of dark brilliance.

Bob clutched the remnants of a shattered half of a white Wheel of Existence—dim, fading into glimmers of ash. He'd used it not just to find the True Source of the Singed, but to bypass its protective folds—a feat that would've obliterated anyone else.
Half of an entire Wheel of Existence began to crumble into pure white ash. With its collapse came the release of countless souls.
Wailing entities—burning within the weavings of a dead True Source for what could have been centuries now perished.
Their cries ceased.
As if they had been released.
Towards the end, the ceasing cries of some even seemed to be those of relief as if they were thankful they did not have to live in death any longer!
A silence came.
And with that silence, Bob's face twisted with grief.
His bald head began to regenerate, flesh knitting back together as his eyes filled with the weight of what he had just done.
For so long, he'd heard those screams. And now...gone. Silenced.
The absence was unbearable.
He nearly screamed.
But he held it in. Because what he'd sacrificed... couldn't be in vain.
His will surged outward across the white-gold landscape of this True Frequency.
He saw the remnants of fallen wheels. He saw a terrifying, silver-white Wheel of Existence—its countless Spokes gleaming like spears.
And he saw the Origin Singed—its expression livid, its body seething with rising power.
The defender placed here within this sacred frequency to ensure that this very scenario never happened.
And yet Bob cast only a single glance toward the Origin Singed before shifting his gaze toward a distant horizon.
A direction where waves of white-gold brilliance stretched on endlessly—seemingly empty.
But Bob felt it.
An entrance.
One that led directly to the Absolute True Source of Existence—the core of the Wheel itself.
BOOM!
He surged forward.
But Noah moved just as fast.

His obsidian form, blazing with the splendor of the True Source of Existence, blinked into Bob's path. He collided with him, driving him back as a Pillar of Concordance sent Bob spiraling across the skies.
Noah turned his gaze toward the distant Origin Singed, hand outstretched, voice roaring:
"Don't you fucking dare bring back your True Source!"
His presence thundered with command. He could already feel it—that sliver of power within the Origin Singed was rising rapidly, nearing the Nascent Source-Bearer level of complexity.
That meant one thing.
The Origin Singed was preparing to recall its True Source from the Infinite Ravines and forcefully reintegrating it into the Wheel of Existence.
It was the same blasphemous action the Omnifather once took—an act that brought Bob, the Dead Thing, into being.
And now, it was happening again.
This ancient being, who lived for logic, purity, and precision, heard Noah's words.
But his expression remained unreadable.
His body launched forward, inserting itself between Bob and the distant entrance.
His voice, ancient and resolute, echoed like a verdict.

"The most important priority is to stop the immediate threat—the one that seeks to disrupt or collapse the Wheel of Existence. That threat is here. It has pierced this sacred place. In its presence, all other possibilities are irrelevant."
Pure logic radiated from him.
From his perspective, if Bob reached the heart of the Wheel, nothing else mattered.
What use was it to protect the Infinite Ravines if a Dead Thing had already broken into a True Frequency of the Wheel itself and was about to taint its Core?
If the Origin Singed's main body remained anchored within its Gateway Domus—what difference would it make?
What was he defending if the core was already compromised?
So, in the next moment—
From a Nascent Source-Bearer Complexity, a terrifying grandeur erupted.
The power of Harmonized Sourcebound Icon Complexity surged from the Origin Singed.
His form warped, appearing before Bob.
A massive Pillar of Concordance, glowing with pure white and gold, bloomed—slamming into Bob and enveloping him completely.
The True Origin Singed had returned.
Abandoning his position. Bearing the weight of unspeakable consequences.
But he returned with his full True Source of Existence...

chapters.title: Chapter 3667 Ashes II
paragraphs: A terrifying Harmonized Sourcebound Icon Complexity erupted before Bob.
The Pillar of Concordance it conjured lashed out, wrapping violently around Bob and burning everything he held as it was unfathomably heavy and seeking to purify and scorch entirely!
Khaos burned.
The remaining half of the white Wheel in his hands began to disintegrate in flickering, golden flames.
And Bob—Bob let out a guttural, broken howl that echoed across frequencies.
"I. JUST. WANT. TO. SAVE. HER!"
HUUM!
The shattered white Wheel pulsed in his grasp, unleashing the wails of countless quintillions of bound souls.
It burned with terrifying brilliance. Bob took the broken Wheel and swung it against the pillar raging around him.
BOOM!
Like a fissure tearing through the very layers of existence, the Pillar of Concordance split—flickering in and out of reality before shattering into oblivion.
Without pause, Bob seized the trembling, ruined Wheel like a spear. His arm swung back before he hurled it- tumultuous, raw, and final...toward the Origin Singed.
OOOH!
A cataclysm of complexity roared as Noah's own True Source of Existence surged forward like a tidal wave- black stellar seas howling through the void.
But it was a beat too slow.
Just a breath too far away.
Because in the moment before Noah's source could sweep the battlefield, the shattered white Wheel struck the chest of the Origin Singed.
BOOM!

A Dead Absolute Complex True Source—shattered though it was—slammed into a freshly returned Origin Singed. The impact hurled him back, his chest splitting open in a torrent of glowing, white-gold blood.
With a livid glare, the Origin Singed tried to pull the embedded Wheel from his chest—but it was like dragging the weight of endless complexity.
It anchored him.
It dragged him down.
Toward the endless white-gold seas below.
And Bob? He surged forward once more.
A Harmonized Sourcebound Icon manifested, the Origin Singed himself...only to be one-shotted by Bob in passing!
It wasn't to discredit the power of the Origin Singed—no.
He was one of the last sentinels left behind by the Wheel to stand in the face of annihilation.
But this enemy?
This enemy was obscene.
Far too obscene for the likes of common weavings to understand!
The Origin Singed had been bound by something no other enemy could conjure: a dead, half-shattered Wheel of Existence.
All he could do was raise his gaze and watch-watch as a Dead Thing neared the Wheel of Existence.
And in that moment, the Origin Singed howled.
"O Singed! Burn all that you have for the sake of the Wheel!"

His voice was thunder and reverence—laced with desperation. All across the void, figures of Singed in various complexities obeyed, bursting into radiant white flames that surged toward him as their expression were heavy. So, so heavy.
All... except two.
Emelline and Mysara stood frozen. Eyes wide.
Trembling.
Their strength... nowhere near enough for this battle, but the commands they followed were not of that Origin Singed!
At such a time—
Because if he didn't stop Bob now, Bob would reach the point of entry that led straight to the Wheel of Existence.
Noah turned to his dwindling seeds of stellar obsidian—the essence of his True Source of Existence.
He knew. He needed more.
More complexity. More power.
Because if he didn't stop Bob now, Bob would reach the point of entry that led straight to the Wheel of Existence.
His weavings buzzed violently—urging, summoning everything he had.
And from the depths of his soul, across all entangled paths...
|Master, I am here.|
The weavings of Ruination surged through him.
That inseparable, unbreakable connection.
And through her... he felt the birth of something terrifying.

|As a Ruined Miniare Wheel of Existence, I should have already been a True Source. But my complexity was too low. After consuming the Pieces and Spokes of the Wheel, I have reached the threshold. It is sufficient. My True Source is yours, Master.|
HUUM!
Her voice—serene and filled with adoration as though she wanted to give him everything she possessed.
And in that moment, she gifted him something wondrous—a spoonful of complexity that exploded through his being.
Prompts rose from the core of his Existence.
|The Pathway to the True Source of Ruination has been traversed by Ruination herself on your behalf.|
|The True Source of Ruination is budding within your Existence as your complexity reaches new heights.|
Ruination.
Wondrously crimson. Fantastically destructive.
Noah closed his eyes.
And though he wouldn't dare speak the depths of his adoration for her—this construct that had stood by him, again and again—he gave her only two words.
'Thank you.'
Just two words were what he uttered!
And across their connection, he felt it.
Her entire being buzzed—as if those words were the greatest gift she had ever received.
In that instant, he was gifted a True Source.
He felt it.
He communed with it.
And though time was cruel and fleeting, he understood enough in the span of an instant.
He understood what Ruination was.
And with his eyes locked on Bob—who was already nearing the edges of his obsidian restraints of the True Source of Existence.
Noah called out.
"Endless Ruin- Infinite Bastille."
A whisper.
And yet, reality responded as if it had been screamed into its bones.
Reality turned red.
Existence bled.
And from every direction, crimson Pillars of Ruin bloomed, encircling Bob. And then, they were gone.
But above and below him, his reality shifted.
Bob was now sealed within a cylindrical crimson prison. No walls. No floor. No ceiling. Just a vertical tunnel of unending red—stretching forever.
Noah watched this unfold, his voice a lullaby of finality.
"No bars. No walls. Just a descent into endless Ruination... until you forget the very notion of rising."
Bob's figure began to fall.
And fall.
Perpetually.
Around him, the weavings of Khaos and a spinning Black Wheel of Existence raged in defiance.
But now—it wasn't all about complexity.
It was about understanding Ruination itself.
Unless one's complexity entirely eclipsed Noah's.
Unless one could shatter the source of Ruination itself.
They would never escape.
This was...
Endless Ruin—Infinite Bastille.
An eternal prison.
A recursive tapestry of existential descent where time loops, and pain multiplies, where dread grows heavier the longer you fall.
Where rising... is no longer a concept!

sentences.text: A terrifying Harmonized Sourcebound Icon Complexity erupted before Bob.
The Pillar of Concordance it conjured lashed out, wrapping violently around Bob and burning everything he held as it was unfathomably heavy and seeking to purify and scorch entirely!
Khaos burned.
The remaining half of the white Wheel in his hands began to disintegrate in flickering, golden flames.
And Bob—Bob let out a guttural, broken howl that echoed across frequencies.
JUST.
WANT.
TO.
SAVE.
HER!"
HUUM!
The shattered white Wheel pulsed in his grasp, unleashing the wails of countless quintillions of bound souls.
It burned with terrifying brilliance.
Bob took the broken Wheel and swung it against the pillar raging around him.
BOOM!
Like a fissure tearing through the very layers of existence, the Pillar of Concordance split—flickering in and out of reality before shattering into oblivion.
Without pause, Bob seized the trembling, ruined Wheel like a spear.
His arm swung back before he hurled it- tumultuous, raw, and final...toward the Origin Singed.
OOOH!
A cataclysm of complexity roared as Noah's own True Source of Existence surged forward like a tidal wave- black stellar seas howling through the void.
But it was a beat too slow.
Just a breath too far away.
Because in the moment before Noah's source could sweep the battlefield, the shattered white Wheel struck the chest of the Origin Singed.
BOOM!
A Dead Absolute Complex True Source—shattered though it was—slammed into a freshly returned Origin Singed.
The impact hurled him back, his chest splitting open in a torrent of glowing, white-gold blood.
With a livid glare, the Origin Singed tried to pull the embedded Wheel from his chest—but it was like dragging the weight of endless complexity.
It anchored him.
It dragged him down.
Toward the endless white-gold seas below.
And Bob?
He surged forward once more.
A Harmonized Sourcebound Icon manifested, the Origin Singed himself...only to be one-shotted by Bob in passing!
It wasn't to discredit the power of the Origin Singed—no.
He was one of the last sentinels left behind by the Wheel to stand in the face of annihilation.
But this enemy?
This enemy was obscene.
Far too obscene for the likes of common weavings to understand!
The Origin Singed had been bound by something no other enemy could conjure: a dead, half-shattered Wheel of Existence.
All he could do was raise his gaze and watch-watch as a Dead Thing neared the Wheel of Existence.
And in that moment, the Origin Singed howled.
"O Singed!
Burn all that you have for the sake of the Wheel!"
His voice was thunder and reverence—laced with desperation.
All across the void, figures of Singed in various complexities obeyed, bursting into radiant white flames that surged toward him as their expression were heavy.
So, so heavy.
All... except two.
Emelline and Mysara stood frozen.
Eyes wide.
Trembling.
Their strength... nowhere near enough for this battle, but the commands they followed were not of that Origin Singed!
At such a time—
Because if he didn't stop Bob now, Bob would reach the point of entry that led straight to the Wheel of Existence.
Noah turned to his dwindling seeds of stellar obsidian—the essence of his True Source of Existence.
He knew.
He needed more.
More complexity.
More power.
Because if he didn't stop Bob now, Bob would reach the point of entry that led straight to the Wheel of Existence.
His weavings buzzed violently—urging, summoning everything he had.
And from the depths of his soul, across all entangled paths...
|Master, I am here.|
The weavings of Ruination surged through him.
That inseparable, unbreakable connection.
And through her... he felt the birth of something terrifying.
|As a Ruined Miniare Wheel of Existence, I should have already been a True Source.
But my complexity was too low.
After consuming the Pieces and Spokes of the Wheel, I have reached the threshold.
It is sufficient.
My True Source is yours, Master.|
HUUM!
Her voice—serene and filled with adoration as though she wanted to give him everything she possessed.
And in that moment, she gifted him something wondrous—a spoonful of complexity that exploded through his being.
Prompts rose from the core of his Existence.
|The Pathway to the True Source of Ruination has been traversed by Ruination herself on your behalf.|
|The True Source of Ruination is budding within your Existence as your complexity reaches new heights.|
Ruination.
Wondrously crimson.
Fantastically destructive.
Noah closed his eyes.
And though he wouldn't dare speak the depths of his adoration for her—this construct that had stood by him, again and again—he gave her only two words.
'Thank you.'
Just two words were what he uttered!
And across their connection, he felt it.
Her entire being buzzed—as if those words were the greatest gift she had ever received.
In that instant, he was gifted a True Source.
He felt it.
He communed with it.
And though time was cruel and fleeting, he understood enough in the span of an instant.
He understood what Ruination was.
And with his eyes locked on Bob—who was already nearing the edges of his obsidian restraints of the True Source of Existence.
Noah called out.
"Endless Ruin- Infinite Bastille."
A whisper.
And yet, reality responded as if it had been screamed into its bones.
Reality turned red.
Existence bled.
And from every direction, crimson Pillars of Ruin bloomed, encircling Bob.
And then, they were gone.
But above and below him, his reality shifted.
Bob was now sealed within a cylindrical crimson prison.
No walls.
No floor.
No ceiling.
Just a vertical tunnel of unending red—stretching forever.
Noah watched this unfold, his voice a lullaby of finality.
"No bars.
No walls.
Just a descent into endless Ruination... until you forget the very notion of rising."
Bob's figure began to fall.
And fall.
Perpetually.
Around him, the weavings of Khaos and a spinning Black Wheel of Existence raged in defiance.
But now—it wasn't all about complexity.
It was about understanding Ruination itself.
Unless one's complexity entirely eclipsed Noah's.
Unless one could shatter the source of Ruination itself.
They would never escape.
This was...
Endless Ruin—Infinite Bastille.
An eternal prison.
A recursive tapestry of existential descent where time loops, and pain multiplies, where dread grows heavier the longer you fall.
Where rising... is no longer a concept!

chapters.title: Chapter 3668 Ashes III
paragraphs: An endless prison.
Bob was falling, physically and existentially, after reaching the True Frequency of the Singed through shocking means.
Noah watched him, sensing the growing burst of complexity within and then spoke aloud.

"You might be able to get out if you shatter the other Dead Absolute Complex True Source of Existence. Or you might not. But if you do, all the cards you have will be lost. The feasibility of even getting close to what you want will be all but gone."
His voice echoed with quiet dread as Bob's form continued plummeting into the Endless Ruin- Infinite Bastille.
Bob's face twisted in anguish, his voice a raw bellow.
"I just want to save her! I...just want her back! Why must Existence itself fight me at every turn?!"
His mind hovered at the brink of collapse, his mental state unraveling at the edges.
Noah stared, his body wrapped in the crimson allure of Ruination. Around him, a Pillar of Concordance of Ruination bloomed as he stood like a warden over the plummeting being.

Elsewhere, another of Noah's bodies that had been perched atop the True Heart of Existence devouring everything it could flashed, now wrapped in obsidian-stellar light, glowing with the True Source of Existence.

He appeared directly above the Origin Singed who was smashed against a remnant Spoke of the Wheel, his chest liquefying in a necrotizing bloom as a shattered half of a white wheel was embedded within him and suppressing his very weavings of existence.
Noah's gaze was cold.
"Your return to the Wheel of Existence...did anything follow you? Did any Dead Thing slip through the Gateway Domus you protected?"
His eyes burned with restrained fury.
The Origin Singed roared his answer as he felt his weavings of existence collapsing.
"Two. Two Dead Things have entered!"
Noah's expression turned soured, his words coming out freely.
"Fucking hell."
In solving one problem, they'd ushered in two more.
The Origin Singed looked to him with a face that mingled power, pain, and a strange apathy.

"The core of the Wheel must be protected. Nothing, not even you, should enter. The Wheel weaves as the Wheel weaves. Since you've stopped that Dead Thing from advancing, perhaps you are now the latest weaving. Protect it. I will..."
His words faltered, his existence crumbling with them.
Noah's voice cut through him like a blade.
"Shut the fuck up and clean up the mess you made."
HUUM!
His hand stretched forth, tendrils of obsidian-stellar light erupting as he grasped the necrotizing shard of the Wheel of Existence.
A black Pillar of Concordance crashed down, engulfing the entire region, bathing the white wheel and the bloodied figure of the pierced Origin Singed.
"Echoes of the Unwritten."
HUUM!
Noah's voice held no warmth as the weavings of Existence burst forth in magnificent wonder.
Power surged- power to undo, to redo- spilling over the Origin Singed. His horrific wounds began to reverse, the embedded white wheel slowly drawing itself out, suspended in air.
But as Noah rewound the attack, his weavings sensed something—a whisper of corruption nestled between the broken white wheel and the healing wound of the Origin Singed.
As the wound sealed, a silent, creeping infection remained- the will of the Great Usurper.
That white fragment... it held countless dead souls, their essences already fading. They had been infected- tainted by the Great Usurper.
And when that Wheel fragment embedded into the Singed, it had carried the Usurper's will straight into him.
Noah did not undo this.
As the wound sealed, a silent, creeping infection remained- the will of the Great Usurper.
Noah turned to the Origin Singed, his tone like frozen steel.
"Let's go fix your mess. Where are the two Dead Things you let through?"
The Origin Singed touched his chest, then cast his gaze toward the blazing crimson prison in the distance of the True Frequency of the Singed pulsing with eerie heat.
"I must protect this frequency before anything else. That is my—"
HUUM!
The very weavings of the True Source of Existence grew heavy around them as Noah stared, unblinking.
The undone weavings that had been vented were now being rewound. The shattered white Wheel of Existence, suspended in a sea of obsidian light, began gravitating back toward the Origin Singed's chest.
The wound reopened.
Necrotizing white bloomed again as the agony returned.
Noah repeated himself, unwavering.
"Let us go and fix your fucking mess."
This time, it wasn't a suggestion.
It was a command.
The Origin Singed felt it- the threat in Noah's voice.
Far away, Emelline of the First Flame and Mysara saw this unfolding and instinctively looked away.
The Origin Singed's expression remained placid as his gaze shifted to the imprisoned Bob, who howled within the Endless folds of Ruination.
He closed his eyes.
"The Wheel weaves as the Wheel weaves."
A reluctant acceptance.
Noah began reversing events once more. The Singed's chest healed fully, the white Wheel fragment retreating further.
But by doing so, Noah silently allowed the will of the Usurper to dig even deeper.
That being wrapped in gold and white flame cast one final look at Bob, then tore space open with his left hand, revealing a massive rift.
He stepped through it.
Noah followed.
They were heading toward the two Dead Things that had passed into the Wheel as consequence of the Singed's return.
What they left behind was a raging stellar obsidian Pillar of Concordance of Existence, containing a shattered white wheel spinning in silence.
What remained were Emelline and Mysara, tending to the thousands of Singed whose existences had been scarred by that one suicidal command- to burn themselves for his cause.
They moved to care for the fallen as their expressions were extremely heavy as if they had to reflect and think back go everything they knew, while behind them...
Noah's other body remained.
Bathed in the crimson weavings of Ruination, standing as sentinel over the imprisoned Bob.
And upon his chest, a wondrous Affix of the Cradle of Purity bloomed, its light shining even as he stared down the Dead Thing trapped in the Endless Ruin.
